at falde.explanation: "At falde" means "to fall", for example to fall down, or for rain and snow to fall: Jeg faldt af cyklen (I fell off the bike).

sentence.da: Der kan **falde** meget sne i nat.
sentence.en: A lot of snow can fall tonight.

at falde for.explanation: "At falde for" means "to fall for", to suddenly like someone or something a lot: Jeg faldt for ham med det samme (I fell for him right away).

sentence.da: Alle vil **falde for** hendes smil.
sentence.en: Everyone will fall for her smile.

at falde i søvn.explanation: "At falde i søvn" means "to fall asleep", the moment you drift off: Hun faldt i søvn i toget (She fell asleep on the train). Being asleep is at sove (to sleep): Hun sover (She is sleeping).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og vil snart **falde i søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and will soon fall asleep.

at falde ned.explanation: "At falde ned" means "to fall down", often from a height: Barnet faldt ned fra træet (The child fell down from the tree). For a fall on the ground, plain at falde (to fall) is common: Han faldt på isen (He fell on the ice).

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **falde ned**!
sentence.en: Be careful, you can fall down!

at falde over.explanation: "At falde over" means "to trip over" something: Jeg faldt over en sten (I tripped over a stone). It can also mean "to come across" something by chance: Jeg faldt over en gammel bog (I came across an old book).

forms.en: I have tripped over / come across

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **falde over** hunden.
sentence.en: I am afraid of tripping over the dog.

at fange.explanation: "At fange" means "to catch" something moving or someone running away: Politiet fanger tyven (The police catch the thief). For a bus or a train, say at nå (to make it): Jeg når toget (I catch the train).

sentence.da: Kan du **fange** bolden, når jeg kaster?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw?

at fare vild.explanation: "At fare vild" means "to get lost", when you do not know where you are: Vi for vild i skoven (We got lost in the forest). To say you lost a thing, use at miste (to lose): Jeg mistede min nøgle (I lost my key).

sentence.da: Uden kort kan vi nemt **fare vild**.
sentence.en: Without a map, we can easily get lost.

at farve.explanation: "At farve" means "to color" or "to dye": Hun farver håret rødt (She dyes her hair red). It also fits coloring in a picture: Børnene farver tegningen (The kids color the drawing).

sentence.da: Hun vil gerne **farve** sit hår rødt.
sentence.en: She would like to dye her hair red.

at feje.explanation: "At feje" means "to sweep", usually with a broom: Jeg fejer gulvet (I sweep the floor). It is for dry dirt like crumbs. Wet cleaning is a different job: Jeg vasker gulvet (I wash the floor).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **feje** køkkenet i dag.
sentence.en: I have to sweep the kitchen today.

at fejle.explanation: "At fejle" means "to fail", and also "to be wrong with": Planen fejlede (The plan failed). Hvad fejler du? (What is wrong with you?) For failing an exam, Danes say at dumpe (to flunk).

sentence.da: Denne plan kan ikke **fejle**.
sentence.en: This plan cannot fail.

at fejre.explanation: "At fejre" means "to celebrate" a day or an event: Vi fejrer jul sammen (We celebrate Christmas together).

sentence.da: Vi vil **fejre** min fødselsdag i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to celebrate my birthday on the weekend.

at feste.explanation: "At feste" means "to party", meaning to go out and celebrate: Vi fester hele natten (We party all night). A party itself is en fest (a party).

sentence.da: Vi vil **feste** hele natten i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to party all night this weekend.

at filme.explanation: "At filme" means "to film": Jeg filmer koncerten (I film the concert). A movie is en film: Vi ser en film (We watch a movie).

sentence.da: Må jeg **filme** dig med min telefon?
sentence.en: May I film you with my phone?

at finde.explanation: "At finde" means "to find", whether you look for something or come across it: Jeg finder mine nøgler (I find my keys). It is also used for opinions: Jeg finder det svært (I find it difficult).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **finde** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I can't find my keys.

at finde på.explanation: "At finde på" means "to come up with", for ideas and made-up things: Vi fandt på en leg (We came up with a game). Plain at finde means "to find": Jeg finder nøglen (I find the key).

sentence.da: Vi skal **finde på** noget sjovt i weekenden.
sentence.en: We have to come up with something fun this weekend.

at finde ud af.explanation: "At finde ud af" means "to find out" and "to figure out": Jeg finder ud af, hvornår toget kører (I find out when the train leaves). Do not mix it up with at finde på (to come up with).

forms.en: I have found out / figured out

sentence.da: Jeg vil **finde ud af**, hvad der er galt.
sentence.en: I want to find out what is wrong.

at finde vej.explanation: "At finde vej" means "to find one's way", to get to the place you are going: Vi finder vej til hotellet (We find our way to the hotel). It is the opposite of at fare vild (to get lost).

sentence.da: Med et kort kan jeg let **finde vej**.
sentence.en: With a map, I can easily find my way.

at fjerne.explanation: "At fjerne" means "to remove": Jeg fjerner billedet fra væggen (I remove the picture from the wall). It is built from fjern (far away), and the same fjern is in en fjernbetjening (a remote control).

sentence.da: Kan du **fjerne** skoene fra bordet?
sentence.en: Can you take the shoes off the table?

at flygte.explanation: "At flygte" means "to flee", to get away from danger: Familien flygtede fra krigen (The family fled the war).

sentence.da: De måtte **flygte** fra deres hjem.
sentence.en: They had to flee from their home.

at flytte.explanation: "At flytte" means "to move", either to a new home or to shift something from one place to another: Vi flytter til Aarhus (We are moving to Aarhus). Kan du flytte bilen? (Can you move the car?)

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte** til et nyt hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move to a new house.

at flytte ind.explanation: "At flytte ind" means "to move in", to start living in a new home: Vi flytter ind på lørdag (We move in on Saturday). Without ind, at flytte means to move something: Jeg flytter bordet (I move the table).

sentence.da: Vi skal **flytte ind** i vores nye hus.
sentence.en: We are going to move into our new house.

at flytte sammen.explanation: "At flytte sammen" means "to move in together": Vi flyttede sammen i maj (We moved in together in May). Sammen (together) is what makes it about sharing a home.

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **flytte sammen** næste år.
sentence.en: We would like to move in together next year.

at flytte sig.explanation: "At flytte sig" means "to move (oneself)", like stepping aside: Kan du flytte dig? (Can you move?) Without sig, at flytte means "to move house" or "to move a thing": Vi flytter til Aarhus (We are moving to Aarhus).

sentence.da: Bilen står i vejen, og han vil ikke **flytte sig**.
sentence.en: The car is in the way, and he won't move.

at flytte ud.explanation: "At flytte ud" means "to move out", to leave a home for good: Min søn flytter ud i august (My son moves out in August). The opposite is at flytte ind (to move in).

sentence.da: Min datter skal **flytte ud** og bo alene.
sentence.en: My daughter is going to move out and live alone.

at flyve.explanation: "At flyve" means "to fly", for birds and for people traveling by plane: Vi flyver til Spanien (We are flying to Spain).

sentence.da: Fuglen kan **flyve** højt.
sentence.en: The bird can fly high.

at fodre.explanation: "At fodre" means "to feed", giving food to someone else, like an animal or a baby: Jeg fodrer hunden (I feed the dog). It is not used for feeding yourself.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **fodre** hundene klokken seks.
sentence.en: I have to feed the dogs at six o'clock.

at folde.explanation: "At folde" means "to fold", for clothes, paper and towels: Hun folder papiret to gange (She folds the paper twice).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **folde** tøjet og lægge det i skabet.
sentence.en: I have to fold the clothes and put them in the closet.

at forandre.explanation: "At forandre" means "to change", making something different: Du har forandret dig (You have changed). To replace one thing with another, use at skifte (to switch): Jeg skifter job (I am changing jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forandre** mit liv i år.
sentence.en: I want to change my life this year.

at forandre sig.explanation: "At forandre sig" means "to change", when someone or something becomes different: Byen har forandret sig (The city has changed). Without sig, it means "to change something": Han forandrer planen (He changes the plan).

sentence.da: Mange ting vil **forandre sig** i fremtiden.
sentence.en: Many things will change in the future.

at forbedre.explanation: "At forbedre" means "to improve", making something better: Vi forbedrer servicen (We are improving the service). It says what you do to something. For something getting better on its own, say at blive bedre (to get better).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **forbedre** mit danske ordforråd.
sentence.en: I would like to improve my Danish vocabulary.

at forberede.explanation: "At forberede" means "to prepare": Hun forbereder middagen (She is preparing dinner). Add sig for yourself: Jeg forbereder mig til prøven (I am getting ready for the test).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **forberede** et møde i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to prepare a meeting tomorrow.

at forberede sig.explanation: "At forberede sig" means "to prepare", getting yourself ready: Jeg forbereder mig til eksamen (I prepare for the exam). Without sig, it means "to prepare something": Hun forbereder et møde (She prepares a meeting).

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **forberede sig** til prøven.
sentence.en: The students have to prepare for the test.

at forbinde.explanation: "At forbinde" means "to connect", and the second thing comes after med (with): Jeg forbinder printeren med computeren (I connect the printer to the computer). It also means "to associate": Jeg forbinder sommer med is (I associate summer with ice cream).

sentence.da: Du kan **forbinde** din telefon med højttaleren.
sentence.en: You can connect your phone to the speaker.

at forbyde.explanation: "At forbyde" means "to forbid" and "to ban": Regeringen forbyder plastikposer (The government bans plastic bags). For a sign, Det er forbudt at ryge her means "Smoking is forbidden here".

sentence.da: Skolen vil **forbyde** mobiler i timerne.
sentence.en: The school wants to ban phones in class.

at foreslå.explanation: "At foreslå" means "to suggest", putting an idea forward for others to accept or turn down. The idea can follow at (that) or come straight after: Jeg foreslår en anden dag (I suggest another day).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **foreslå**, at vi spiser ude.
sentence.en: I want to suggest that we eat out.

at forestille sig.explanation: "At forestille sig" means "to imagine": Jeg kan ikke forestille mig det (I cannot imagine that). Sig changes with who imagines: mig for jeg (I), dig for du (you).

sentence.da: Hun kan ikke **forestille sig** livet uden musik.
sentence.en: She cannot imagine life without music.

at foretrække.explanation: "At foretrække" means "to prefer": Hun foretrækker at gå (She prefers to walk). To say what you like less, add frem for (over): Jeg foretrækker hunde frem for katte (I prefer dogs to cats).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **foretrække** te frem for kaffe.
sentence.en: I would prefer tea to coffee.

at forhandle.explanation: "At forhandle" means "to negotiate", for example prices, contracts or pay. You negotiate about something with om (about): forhandle om prisen (negotiate the price). Be careful: en forhandler is not a negotiator but a dealer or retailer, such as a car dealer.

sentence.da: Vi vil **forhandle** om prisen.
sentence.en: We want to negotiate the price.

at forhindre.explanation: "At forhindre" means "to prevent", stopping something from happening: Vaccinen forhindrer sygdom (The vaccine prevents illness). With a person, add i at (from) before the action: Regnen forhindrede os i at gå (The rain stopped us from going).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forhindre** mange ulykker med bedre veje.
sentence.en: We can prevent many accidents with better roads.

at forklare.explanation: "At forklare" means "to explain". Danish says forklare noget for nogen (explain something to someone): Kan du forklare det for mig? (Can you explain it to me?).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **forklare** ordet.
sentence.en: The teacher will explain the word.

at forlade.explanation: "At forlade" means "to leave" a place or a person: Hun forlod huset kl. 8 (She left the house at 8). Hun forlod ham (She left him). For simply going away, use at gå (to go): Jeg går nu (I am leaving now).

sentence.da: Han vil **forlade** landet i næste måned.
sentence.en: He will leave the country next month.

at forlove sig.explanation: "At forlove sig" means "to get engaged", the promise to marry someone before the wedding. The person you get engaged to comes after med (with): Hun forlovede sig med Peter i sommer (She got engaged to Peter last summer).

sentence.da: Han har en ring og vil **forlove sig** med hende.
sentence.en: He has a ring and wants to get engaged to her.

at forsinke.explanation: "At forsinke" means "to delay", making something late: Snevejret forsinker toget (The snowstorm delays the train). The train itself is forsinket (delayed): Toget er forsinket (The train is delayed).

sentence.da: Trafikken kan **forsinke** os med en time.
sentence.en: The traffic can delay us by an hour.

at forstyrre.explanation: "At forstyrre" means "to disturb": Jeg vil ikke forstyrre dig (I do not want to disturb you). To ask politely when you walk in, say Må jeg forstyrre? (May I interrupt?)

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **forstyrre** hende, når hun arbejder.
sentence.en: The children must not disturb her when she works.

at forstå.explanation: "At forstå" means "to understand": Jeg forstår ikke (I don't understand). To say you know a fact, use at vide (to know) instead: Jeg ved det ikke (I don't know).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **forstå** ham.
sentence.en: I cannot understand him.

at forsvinde.explanation: "At forsvinde" means "to disappear" or "to vanish": Solen forsvandt bag skyerne (The sun disappeared behind the clouds).

sentence.da: Tyven kan **forsvinde** i mængden.
sentence.en: The thief can disappear in the crowd.

at forsøge.explanation: "At forsøge" means "to attempt" or "to try": Jeg forsøger at forstå (I am trying to understand). Unlike at prøve (to try), it is not used for trying out or tasting: Jeg prøver kagen (I try the cake).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **forsøge** at komme i morgen.
sentence.en: I will try to come tomorrow.

at fortjene.explanation: "At fortjene" means "to deserve": Du fortjener en pause (You deserve a break). It is built on at tjene (to earn), but earning money uses tjene alone: Jeg tjener penge (I earn money).

sentence.da: Hun har trænet hårdt og kan **fortjene** prisen.
sentence.en: She has trained hard and may deserve the prize.

at fortryde.explanation: "At fortryde" means "to regret": Jeg fortryder det ikke (I do not regret it). To say what you regret, add at (that): Jeg fortryder, at jeg sagde det (I regret that I said it).

sentence.da: Du kommer til at **fortryde** det senere.
sentence.en: You will regret it later.

at fortsætte.explanation: "At fortsætte" means "to continue": Vi fortsætter i morgen (We continue tomorrow). To keep doing something, add med at (-ing): Fortsæt med at læse! (Keep reading!)

sentence.da: Efter pausen kan vi **fortsætte** timen.
sentence.en: After the break, we can continue the class.

at fortsætte med.explanation: "At fortsætte med" means "to continue with" something you are already doing: Vi fortsætter med lektionen (We continue with the lesson). To just keep going, say Fortsæt! (Keep going!).

sentence.da: Vi kan **fortsætte med** øvelsen efter pausen.
sentence.en: We can continue with the exercise after the break.

at fortælle.explanation: "At fortælle" means "to tell", especially to tell a story or give someone information: Han fortæller om sin rejse (He tells about his trip). For simply saying a few words, use at sige (to say): Han siger hej (He says hello). You can add who you tell: fortælle nogen noget (tell someone something).

sentence.da: Min mormor vil **fortælle** en historie til børnene.
sentence.en: My grandmother will tell the children a story.

at forvente.explanation: "At forvente" means "to expect", when you think something will happen: Jeg forventer et svar snart (I expect an answer soon). It can also mean requiring something of someone: Vi forventer, at du kommer til tiden (We expect you to be on time).

sentence.da: Vi kan **forvente** regn i morgen.
sentence.en: We can expect rain tomorrow.

at forværre.explanation: "At forværre" means "to worsen", making something worse: Regnen forværrer trafikken (The rain makes the traffic worse). It is the opposite of at forbedre (to improve).

sentence.da: Dårlig søvn kan **forværre** smerterne.
sentence.en: Poor sleep can worsen the pain.

at fotografere.explanation: "At fotografere" means "to photograph": Jeg fotograferer huset (I photograph the house). Danes more often say at tage et billede af (to take a picture of): Jeg tager et billede af huset (I take a picture of the house).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **fotografere** solnedgangen med min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to photograph the sunset with my phone.

at fri.explanation: "At fri" means "to propose", as in asking someone to marry you. The person you ask comes after til (to): Han friede til hende (He proposed to her).

sentence.da: Han vil **fri** til hende i aften.
sentence.en: He is going to propose to her tonight.

at frygte.explanation: "At frygte" means "to fear", which sounds more serious than being scared: De frygter det værste (They fear the worst). For everyday fear, Danes say at være bange for (to be afraid of): Jeg er bange for hunde (I am afraid of dogs).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke **frygte** fremtiden.
sentence.en: We must not fear the future.

at fryse.explanation: "At fryse" means "to freeze" and also "to feel cold": Jeg fryser (I am cold, literally I freeze). It also describes water turning to ice: Vandet fryser (The water freezes). Do not mix it up with en fryser (a freezer).

sentence.da: Uden jakke vil du **fryse**.
sentence.en: Without a jacket you will freeze.

at fungere.explanation: "At fungere" means "to work", when a thing does what it should: Min telefon fungerer ikke (My phone does not work). For a person at a job, use at arbejde (to work).

sentence.da: Tror du, at planen kan **fungere**?
sentence.en: Do you think the plan can work?

at fylde.explanation: "At fylde" means "to fill": Jeg fylder glasset med vand (I fill the glass with water). It also means "to take up space": Sofaen fylder meget (The sofa takes up a lot of space). For a birthday, it means "to turn": Jeg fylder 30 i dag (I turn 30 today).

forms.en: I have filled / taken up space

sentence.da: Børnene må **fylde** posen med slik.
sentence.en: The children may fill the bag with candy.

at fylde op.explanation: "At fylde op" means "to fill up". Op (up) says you fill it to the top, so it is more complete than plain at fylde (to fill): Jeg fylder kanden op (I fill up the pitcher).

sentence.da: Vi skal **fylde op** med benzin i morgen.
sentence.en: We have to fill up with gas tomorrow.

at fylde år.explanation: "At fylde år" means "to have a birthday", in the sense of turning a certain age. You can add the age: Jeg fylder tredive år (I am turning thirty). At have fødselsdag (to have a birthday) just says it is your birthday, without the age.

sentence.da: Min far skal **fylde år** i morgen.
sentence.en: My dad has a birthday tomorrow.

at fyre.explanation: "At fyre" means "to fire" someone from a job: Chefen fyrede ham (The boss fired him). It also means "to make a fire": Vi fyrer i brændeovnen (We light the wood stove).

sentence.da: Firmaet må **fyre** ti medarbejdere.
sentence.en: The company has to fire ten employees.

at få.explanation: "At få" means "to get" or "to receive": Jeg får et brev (I get a letter). It also appears in få lov (to be allowed): Jeg fik lov (I was allowed). It does not mean to go and fetch something; for that, use at hente (to fetch).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få** en gave til min fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I am going to get a present for my birthday.

at få besked.explanation: "At få besked" means "to be notified", to hear what is going on: Jeg fik besked om mødet (I was told about the meeting). The person who tells you uses at give besked (to let someone know).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **få besked**, når pakken kommer.
sentence.en: I will be notified when the package arrives.

at få besøg.explanation: "At få besøg" means "to have visitors", when someone comes to see you: Vi får besøg i weekenden (We have visitors this weekend). To go see someone yourself, say at være på besøg (to be visiting): Jeg er på besøg hos min mor (I am visiting my mother).

sentence.da: Jeg rydder op, fordi jeg skal **få besøg**.
sentence.en: I am tidying up because I am having guests.

at få det bedre.explanation: "At få det bedre" means "to feel better" after being sick or sad: Jeg håber, du får det bedre (I hope you feel better). To wish someone well, say God bedring! (Get well soon!)

sentence.da: Med lidt hvile vil du **få det bedre**.
sentence.en: With some rest, you will feel better.

at få et barn.explanation: "At få et barn" means "to have a baby", literally to get a child: Vi får et barn i maj (We are having a baby in May).

sentence.da: Min søster er gravid og skal **få et barn**.
sentence.en: My sister is pregnant and is going to have a baby.

at få fat i.explanation: "At få fat i" means "to get hold of", for grabbing a thing or reaching a person: Jeg fik fat i rebet (I grabbed the rope). Jeg kunne ikke få fat i ham (I could not reach him).

sentence.da: Barnet kan ikke **få fat i** kagen på hylden.
sentence.en: The child cannot get hold of the cake on the shelf.

at få fri.explanation: "At få fri" means "to get off", to be allowed to leave work or school: Vi får fri klokken tre (We get off at three). When you decide to take a day yourself, use at tage fri (to take time off).

forms.en: I have gotten off (work or school)

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **få fri** tidligt i dag.
sentence.en: I would like to get off early today.

at få hjælp.explanation: "At få hjælp" means "to get help": Kan jeg få hjælp? (Can I get help?). Danish says hjælp (help) with no en (a) in front: Jeg har brug for hjælp (I need help).

sentence.da: Jeg er syg og vil **få hjælp**.
sentence.en: I am sick and want to get help.

at få lov til.explanation: "At få lov til" means "to be allowed to", when someone gives you permission: Jeg fik lov til at gå hjem (I was allowed to go home).

sentence.da: Børnene vil gerne **få lov til** at blive længe.
sentence.en: The children would like to be allowed to stay longer.

at få lyst til.explanation: "At få lyst til" means "to feel like", when a wish suddenly appears: Jeg fik lyst til kage (I felt like having cake). Before an action, add at (to): Jeg fik lyst til at gå en tur (I felt like going for a walk).

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, kan man **få lyst til** is.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, you can feel like having ice cream.

at få nok.explanation: "At få nok" means "to have had enough", or "to get fed up": Nu har jeg fået nok! (Now I have had enough!) It can also be about food: Har du fået nok at spise? (Have you had enough to eat?)

forms.en: I get fed up (have had enough)

sentence.da: Jeg begynder at **få nok** af støjen.
sentence.en: I am starting to get fed up with the noise.

at få ondt af.explanation: "At få ondt af" means "to feel sorry for" someone: Jeg får ondt af hende (I feel sorry for her). Do not mix it up with at have ondt i (to hurt in): Jeg har ondt i maven (My stomach hurts).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke andet end **få ondt af** ham.
sentence.en: You cannot help feeling sorry for him.

at få ret.explanation: "At få ret" means "to be proven right": Jeg fik ret (I was proven right). Being right is at have ret: Du har ret (You are right).

sentence.da: Jeg tror, hun vil **få ret** til sidst.
sentence.en: I think she will be proven right in the end.

at få styr på.explanation: "At få styr på" means "to get control of", or "to sort out", something messy: Jeg skal få styr på min økonomi (I must sort out my finances). The result is at have styr på (to have it under control).

forms.en: to get control of / sort out
I get control of / sort out
I got control of / sorted out
I have gotten control of / sorted out

sentence.da: Vi skal **få styr på** rodet i garagen.
sentence.en: We have to sort out the mess in the garage.

at få tid.explanation: "At få tid" means "to find time": Jeg fik tid til at læse (I found time to read). It also means "to get an appointment", for example at the doctor or the hairdresser. To be free right now, use at have tid (to have time).

related.en: to have time to / make it

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få tid** hos lægen før mandag.
sentence.en: I can't get an appointment with the doctor before Monday.

at få travlt.explanation: "At få travlt" means "to get busy": Vi fik travlt i går (We got busy yesterday). When you are already busy, use at have travlt: Jeg har travlt (I am busy).

sentence.da: Vi vil **få travlt**, når gæsterne kommer.
sentence.en: We will get busy when the guests arrive.

at få øje på.explanation: "At få øje på" means "to catch sight of", the moment you first notice something: Jeg fik øje på en ræv (I spotted a fox). It is about the first glimpse, not just looking.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **få øje på** bussen endnu.
sentence.en: I can't spot the bus yet.

at fødes.explanation: "At fødes" means "to be born", but in everyday speech people say at blive født (to become born): Jeg blev født i 1990 (I was born in 1990).

sentence.da: Vores barn skal **fødes** i maj.
sentence.en: Our child is due to be born in May.

at føle.explanation: "At føle" means "to feel", both emotions and things you touch. To say how you feel, add mig (me): Jeg føler mig glad means "I feel happy".

sentence.da: Jeg kan **føle** vinden på min hud.
sentence.en: I can feel the wind on my skin.

at føle sig.explanation: "At føle sig" means "to feel (a certain way)" and is followed by a word like glad (happy): Jeg føler mig glad (I feel happy). Sig changes with the person: du føler dig (you feel), han føler sig (he feels).

sentence.da: Man kan **føle sig** ensom i en ny by.
sentence.en: You can feel lonely in a new city.

at føles.explanation: "At føles" means "to feel", about how something seems to you: Vandet føles koldt (The water feels cold). When a person feels, say Jeg føler mig træt (I feel tired).

sentence.da: Det kan **føles** underligt at flytte.
sentence.en: It can feel strange to move.

at følge.explanation: "At følge" means "to follow" a person, a road or a rule: Hunden følger mig (The dog follows me). It also means "to go along with", like walking someone somewhere: Jeg følger dig hjem (I will walk you home).

sentence.da: Alle skal **følge** reglerne i skolen.
sentence.en: Everyone has to follow the rules at school.

at følge med.explanation: "At følge med" means "to keep up" and "to come along": Kan du følge med? (Can you keep up?) Jeg følger med (I'll come along). Plain at følge means "to follow".

forms.en: I have kept up / come along

sentence.da: Hun går hurtigt, og jeg kan ikke **følge med**.
sentence.en: She walks fast, and I can't keep up.

at føre.explanation: "At føre" means "to lead" and "to conduct": Han fører samtalen (He is leading the conversation). It also means "to keep" accounts or records: Vi fører regnskab (We keep the accounts).

sentence.da: Vejen kan **føre** dig til stranden.
sentence.en: The road can lead you to the beach.

en fabrik.explanation: "En fabrik" means "a factory", where things are made in large amounts.

sentence.da: Min bror arbejder på en **fabrik** og laver møbler.
sentence.en: My brother works at a factory and makes furniture.

en familie.explanation: "En familie" means "a family", the people closest to you, such as parents, children, brothers and sisters.

sentence.da: Min **familie** er mor, far og søster.
sentence.en: My family is my mom, my dad and my sister.

en familiefest.explanation: "En familiefest" means "a family party", where relatives come together for a birthday or another special day.

sentence.da: Vi holder en **familiefest** for farmor.
sentence.en: We are having a family party for grandma.

en fan.explanation: "En fan" means "a fan", someone who loves a team, singer or band. For a fan that cools a room, use en ventilator (a fan).

sentence.da: Min bror er **fan** af det danske landshold.
sentence.en: My brother is a fan of the Danish national team.

en fantasi.explanation: "En fantasi" means "an imagination" or "a fantasy". It is the ability to imagine things. It is also something imagined that is not real: Det er bare en fantasi (It is just a fantasy).

sentence.da: Børn har ofte meget **fantasi**.
sentence.en: Children often have a lot of imagination.

en far.explanation: "En far" means "a father". Danish uses far for both father and dad, and children also use it as a name: Hej, far! (Hi, Dad!).

sentence.da: Min mor og min **far** har to børn.
sentence.en: My mother and my father have two children.

en farbror.explanation: "En farbror" means "an uncle", your father's brother. Your mother's brother is en morbror (an uncle).

sentence.da: Min **farbror** er min fars bror og bor i Aarhus.
sentence.en: My uncle is my father's brother and lives in Aarhus.

en fare.explanation: "En fare" means "a danger". Fare for means "danger of": Der er fare for brand (There is a danger of fire).

sentence.da: Børnene er i **fare** på den tynde is.
sentence.en: The children are in danger on the thin ice.

en farfar.explanation: "En farfar" means "a grandfather" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and far (father): father's father. On your mother's side he is en morfar (mother's father).

sentence.da: Min **farfar** er min fars far.
sentence.en: My grandfather is my father's father.

en farmor.explanation: "En farmor" means "a grandmother" on your father's side. It is built from far (father) and mor (mother): father's mother. You can call her farmor directly: Farmor kommer i dag (Grandma is coming today).

sentence.da: Min **farmor** er min fars mor.
sentence.en: My grandmother is my father's mother.

en fart.explanation: "En fart" means "a speed", how quickly something moves. It is also used for pace and energy: Der er fart på (Things are really moving).

sentence.da: Bilen kørte i høj **fart** gennem byen.
sentence.en: The car drove at high speed through the town.

en fartbøde.explanation: "En fartbøde" means "a speeding ticket", the fine for driving too fast. It is built from fart (speed) and bøde (fine). Bøde can stand alone: Jeg fik en bøde (I got a fine).

sentence.da: Han fik en **fartbøde** på motorvejen.
sentence.en: He got a speeding ticket on the highway.

en fartgrænse.explanation: "En fartgrænse" means "a speed limit". If you go too fast, you break it: at overskride fartgrænsen (to exceed the speed limit).

sentence.da: Der er en **fartgrænse** på 50 i byen.
sentence.en: There is a speed limit of 50 in town.

en farve.explanation: "En farve" means "a color", the look of something that you can name, such as the shade of a shirt or a wall.

sentence.da: Hvilken **farve** har din bil? Den er rød.
sentence.en: What color is your car? It is red.

en fase.explanation: "En fase" means "a phase", a part of a process or of someone's life that has its own character and later ends.

sentence.da: Barnet er i en svær **fase** lige nu.
sentence.en: The child is in a hard phase right now.

en fastelavnsbolle.explanation: "En fastelavnsbolle" means "a Shrovetide bun", a sweet bun with cream and icing that Danes eat around Fastelavn, a February holiday when children dress up in costumes.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **fastelavnsbolle** med fløde.
sentence.en: I am eating a Shrovetide bun with cream.

en faster.explanation: "En faster" means "an aunt", your father's sister. Your mother's sister is en moster (an aunt).

sentence.da: Min **faster** er min fars søster og bor i Aalborg.
sentence.en: My aunt is my father's sister and lives in Aalborg.

en favorit.explanation: "En favorit" means "a favorite", the one you like best. It also starts compounds like favoritmad (favorite food).

sentence.da: Pizza er min **favorit** blandt alle retter.
sentence.en: Pizza is my favorite of all dishes.

en feber.explanation: "En feber" means "a fever", a high body temperature when you are sick. Danes say Jeg har feber (I have a fever), usually without en.

sentence.da: Hun har **feber** og bliver i sengen.
sentence.en: She has a fever and stays in bed.

en fejebakke.explanation: "En fejebakke" means "a dustpan", the small flat tray you sweep dust into. It is built from at feje (to sweep) and en bakke (a tray). En bakke also means "a hill", as in en stor bakke (a big hill).

sentence.da: Jeg samler støvet op med en **fejebakke**.
sentence.en: I pick up the dust with a dustpan.

en fejl.explanation: "En fejl" means "an error" or "a bug", and also "a mistake": Der er en fejl i programmet (There is an error in the program). Jeg lavede en fejl (I made a mistake).

sentence.da: Jeg fandt en **fejl** i din tekst.
sentence.en: I found a mistake in your text.

en ferie.explanation: "En ferie" means "a vacation" or holiday, a time away from work or school. You say på ferie (on vacation). I ferien means "during the vacation".

sentence.da: Jeg har fri og tager på **ferie**.
sentence.en: I have time off and am going on vacation.

en fersken.explanation: "En fersken" means "a peach", a round fruit with soft, fuzzy skin.

sentence.da: En **fersken** er sød og saftig, og den har en sten.
sentence.en: A peach is sweet and juicy, and it has a pit.

en fest.explanation: "En fest" means "a party" or a celebration. You say at holde fest (to have a party) or at gå til fest (to go to a party). God fest! means "Have a good party!".

sentence.da: Vi holder **fest** med musik og kage.
sentence.en: We are having a party with music and cake.

en festival.explanation: "En festival" means "a festival", usually for music or film.

sentence.da: Vi skal på **festival** i sommer og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We are going to a festival this summer and sleeping in a tent.

en festsal.explanation: "En festsal" means "a banquet hall", a big room for parties, weddings and school events.

sentence.da: Bryllupsgæsterne spiser og danser i den store **festsal**.
sentence.en: The wedding guests eat and dance in the big banquet hall.

en festtale.explanation: "En festtale" means "a celebratory speech", given by someone at a party. It is built from fest (party) and tale (speech). Danish uses at holde (to hold) for giving a speech: at holde en tale (to give a speech).

sentence.da: Hun holdt en kort **festtale** for sin bedste ven.
sentence.en: She gave a short speech for her best friend.

en figur.explanation: "En figur" means "a figure", such as a shape, a drawing or a character in a story: en figur i bogen (a character in the book). It also means a person's body shape: Hun har en flot figur (She has a nice figure).

sentence.da: Børnene tegner en sjov **figur** på papiret.
sentence.en: The children draw a funny figure on the paper.

en fil.explanation: "En fil" means "a file" on a computer. It is also a metal tool for smoothing things, like en neglefil (a nail file).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne den **fil**, du sendte mig.
sentence.en: I cannot open the file you sent me.

en film.explanation: "En film" means "a film" or "a movie". More than one is also "film": to film means two films (to is the number two). At se en film means "to watch a film".

sentence.da: Vi ser en **film** i biografen.
sentence.en: We watch a film at the cinema.

en filmaften.explanation: "En filmaften" means "a movie night", a night in watching films, often at home with friends. I aften means "tonight", as in Skal vi have filmaften i aften? (Shall we have movie night tonight?)

sentence.da: Vi har **filmaften** hver fredag med popcorn og venner.
sentence.en: We have a movie night every Friday with popcorn and friends.

en filmstjerne.explanation: "En filmstjerne" means "a film star", a famous person from the movies. It is built from film (movie) and stjerne (star). Stjerne is also a star in the sky: Der er mange stjerner i aften (There are many stars tonight).

sentence.da: Hun er blevet en kendt **filmstjerne** i USA.
sentence.en: She has become a famous film star in the USA.

en finger.explanation: "En finger" means "a finger". The thumb is tommelfinger and the index finger is pegefinger. Danish says the finger where English says my finger: Jeg har ondt i fingeren means "I have a pain in the finger", i.e., my finger hurts.

sentence.da: Hun har en ring på sin **finger**.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en firewall.explanation: "En firewall" means "a firewall", a protection that blocks unwanted visitors on a computer or an internet connection.

sentence.da: Min **firewall** stopper farlige programmer.
sentence.en: My firewall stops dangerous programs.

en firkant.explanation: "En firkant" means "a four-sided shape", built from fire (four) and kant (edge). It is any shape with four sides, like a rectangle, while et kvadrat (a square) has four equal sides.

sentence.da: Bordet er en **firkant**, ikke en cirkel.
sentence.en: The table is a four-sided shape, not a circle.

en fisk.explanation: "En fisk" means "a fish", both the animal in the water and the food on your plate. The plural can be the same word as the single one: tre fisk (three fish).

sentence.da: En **fisk** svømmer i vandet.
sentence.en: A fish swims in the water.

en fiskehandler.explanation: "En fiskehandler" means "a fishmonger", the person who sells fresh fish. The word also means the shop itself, so you buy fish hos (at) fiskehandleren.

sentence.da: Jeg køber frisk laks hos en **fiskehandler**.
sentence.en: I buy fresh salmon from a fishmonger.

en fisker.explanation: "En fisker" means "a fisherman", someone who catches fish as a job. The same word is used for men and women.

sentence.da: Vores nabo er **fisker** og sejler hver morgen.
sentence.en: Our neighbor is a fisherman and sails every morning.

en fiskerby.explanation: "En fiskerby" means "a fishing village", a small community by the sea where people make their living from fishing.

sentence.da: Jeg bor i en lille **fiskerby** ved havet.
sentence.en: I live in a small fishing village by the sea.

en fjende.explanation: "En fjende" means "an enemy", someone who is against you, in a war or in everyday life. Hun har ikke en eneste fjende (She does not have a single enemy).

sentence.da: Kongen sendte soldater mod sin **fjende**.
sentence.en: The king sent soldiers against his enemy.

en fjer.explanation: "En fjer" means "a feather". It can also mean the soft filling in a pillow or duvet: en pude med fjer (a pillow with feathers).

sentence.da: Fuglen har en lang **fjer** på vingen.
sentence.en: The bird has a long feather on its wing.

en fjerdedel.explanation: "En fjerdedel" means "a quarter", one of four equal parts. It is built from fjerde (fourth) and del (part), the same way as en femtedel (a fifth).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler en **fjerdedel** af huslejen.
sentence.en: I pay a quarter of the rent.

en fjernbetjening.explanation: "En fjernbetjening" means "a remote control", a small device you use to control something from a distance. It is built from fjern (far) and betjening (operation). Betjening also means "service", as in god betjening (good service).

sentence.da: Man bruger en **fjernbetjening** til at skifte kanal.
sentence.en: You use a remote control to change channels.

en fjord.explanation: "En fjord" means "a fjord", a long, narrow stretch of water that reaches into the land.

sentence.da: Skibet sejler ind i en **fjord**, ikke ud på havet.
sentence.en: The ship sails into a fjord, not out to sea.

en flaske.explanation: "En flaske" means "a bottle". Danish has no word for "of" here: en flaske vand is a bottle of water, and "et glas vand" is a glass of water.

sentence.da: Han hælder mælk fra en **flaske** i glasset.
sentence.en: He pours milk from a bottle into the glass.

en flaskeåbner.explanation: "En flaskeåbner" means "a bottle opener", a tool that pops the metal cap off a bottle. It is built from flaske (bottle) and åbner (opener).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke åbne flasken uden en **flaskeåbner**.
sentence.en: I cannot open the bottle without a bottle opener.

en flirt.explanation: "En flirt" means "a flirt", a playful moment of romantic interest between two people. The action of flirting is at flirte (to flirt).

sentence.da: Det var bare en **flirt**, ikke et rigtigt forhold.
sentence.en: It was just a flirt, not a real relationship.

en flise.explanation: "En flise" means "a tile", a hard, flat square used for floors and walls, most often in kitchens and bathrooms.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger en ny **flise** på badeværelsets gulv.
sentence.en: I am laying a new tile on the bathroom floor.

en flod.explanation: "En flod" means "a river", bigger than en å (a stream).

sentence.da: Der ligger en gammel by ved en bred **flod**.
sentence.en: An old town lies by a wide river.

en flok.explanation: "En flok" means "a flock" or "a crowd", for animals and for people: en flok får (a flock of sheep), en flok børn (a crowd of children).

sentence.da: En **flok** fugle sidder på taget.
sentence.en: A flock of birds is sitting on the roof.

en flue.explanation: "En flue" means "a fly", the small buzzing animal that lands on food. A bigger one that bites is en bremse (a horsefly).

sentence.da: Der er en **flue** i min suppe.
sentence.en: There is a fly in my soup.

en flybillet.explanation: "En flybillet" means "a plane ticket". It is built from fly (plane) and billet (ticket). Billet works for any ticket, like en koncertbillet (a concert ticket).

sentence.da: Uden en **flybillet** kan du ikke flyve.
sentence.en: Without a plane ticket you cannot fly.

en flygtning.explanation: "En flygtning" means "a refugee", a person who has left their country to be safe. The word comes from at flygte (to flee).

sentence.da: Hun kom til Danmark som **flygtning** i 2015.
sentence.en: She came to Denmark as a refugee in 2015.

en flyrejse.explanation: "En flyrejse" means "a flight" as a whole journey by plane. For the plane itself, use et fly: Flyet er forsinket (The plane is delayed).

sentence.da: En **flyrejse** til Spanien tager tre timer.
sentence.en: A flight to Spain takes three hours.

en flytning.explanation: "En flytning" means "a move" from one home to another, not a trip. It comes from at flytte (to move).

sentence.da: Ved en **flytning** pakker man alle sine ting i kasser.
sentence.en: In a move you pack all your things in boxes.

en flyttekasse.explanation: "En flyttekasse" means "a moving box", a sturdy cardboard box for carrying your things. It is built from at flytte (to move) and en kasse (a box). Kasse also means the checkout in a shop: Betal ved kassen (Pay at the checkout).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker alle bøgerne i en **flyttekasse**.
sentence.en: I pack all the books in a moving box.

en flyvetid.explanation: "En flyvetid" means "a flight time", how long a flight takes in the air. It is built from at flyve (to fly) and en tid (a time). En tid also means "an appointment", as in en tid hos lægen (an appointment with the doctor).

sentence.da: Til London er der kun to timers **flyvetid**.
sentence.en: To London there are only two hours of flight time.

en fløjte.explanation: "En fløjte" means both "a flute" and "a whistle": Hun spiller på fløjte (She plays the flute). Dommeren blæser i fløjten (The referee blows the whistle).

sentence.da: Hun spiller **fløjte** i skolens orkester.
sentence.en: She plays the flute in the school orchestra.

en fod.explanation: "En fod" means "a foot". Til fods means on foot (walking). Danish often says the feet where English says my feet: Jeg har ondt i fødderne means my feet hurt (literally I have a pain in the feet).

sentence.da: Skoen er for lille til min **fod**.
sentence.en: The shoe is too small for my foot.

en fodboldkamp.explanation: "En fodboldkamp" means "a soccer match". It is built from fodbold (soccer) and kamp (match). Fodbold is not American football.

sentence.da: Vi ser en **fodboldkamp** på tv i aften.
sentence.en: We are watching a soccer match on TV tonight.

en fodboldspiller.explanation: "En fodboldspiller" means "a soccer player". It is built from fodbold (soccer) and spiller (player). Fodbold is soccer, not American football.

sentence.da: En **fodboldspiller** løber efter bolden og skyder mål.
sentence.en: A soccer player runs after the ball and scores goals.

en fodgænger.explanation: "En fodgænger" means "a pedestrian", literally a foot-goer, from fod (foot).

sentence.da: En **fodgænger** skal vente, når lyset er rødt.
sentence.en: A pedestrian has to wait when the light is red.

en fodgængerzone.explanation: "En fodgængerzone" means "a pedestrian zone", a street area where cars are not allowed.

sentence.da: Der må ikke køre biler i en **fodgængerzone**.
sentence.en: Cars may not drive in a pedestrian zone.

en fodring.explanation: "En fodring" means "a feeding", the time when animals get their food. It comes from at fodre (to give an animal its food).

sentence.da: Dyrene får mad ved hver **fodring**.
sentence.en: The animals get food at each feeding.

en folkeskole.explanation: "En folkeskole" means "a primary school", but it covers all of public school, from about age 6 to 16.

sentence.da: Min søn går i **folkeskole** og har mange venner.
sentence.en: My son goes to primary school and has many friends.

en forandring.explanation: "En forandring" means "a change", often a big one in someone's life, like a new job or a new home. The action is at forandre (to make different).

sentence.da: Efter ti år på kontoret vil jeg have en **forandring**.
sentence.en: After ten years at the office I want a change.

en forbindelse.explanation: "En forbindelse" means "a connection", for internet or phone. It also means a tie between two things: Der er en forbindelse mellem søvn og humør (There is a connection between sleep and mood).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen **forbindelse** til internettet lige nu.
sentence.en: I have no connection to the internet right now.

en forbinding.explanation: "En forbinding" means "a dressing", the soft cloth you wrap around a wound. A small sticky one is et plaster (a Band-Aid).

sentence.da: Han fik en **forbinding** på armen.
sentence.en: He got a dressing on his arm.

en forbryder.explanation: "En forbryder" means "a criminal", a person who breaks the law. It comes from forbrydelse (a crime).

sentence.da: Politiet har fanget en farlig **forbryder**.
sentence.en: The police have caught a dangerous criminal.

en fordel.explanation: "En fordel" means "an advantage" or "a benefit". The opposite is en ulempe (a disadvantage).

sentence.da: Det er en **fordel** at bo tæt på arbejde.
sentence.en: It is an advantage to live close to work.

en forening.explanation: "En forening" means "an association" or "a club", a group of people who meet regularly for a shared purpose.

sentence.da: I en **forening** mødes folk med samme interesse.
sentence.en: In an association, people with the same interest meet.

en forestilling.explanation: "En forestilling" means "a performance", a show for an audience. It can also mean "an idea": Jeg har ingen forestilling om det (I have no idea).

sentence.da: Børnene så en sjov **forestilling** i går.
sentence.en: The children saw a funny show yesterday.

en forfader.explanation: "En forfader" means "an ancestor", a family member who lived long ago. It is built from for (before) and fader (father). Do not mix it up with forældre (parents).

sentence.da: Min **forfader** boede her for længe siden.
sentence.en: My ancestor lived here long ago.

en forfatter.explanation: "En forfatter" means "an author", someone who writes books. The same word is used for men and women.

sentence.da: Hun er **forfatter** og har skrevet tre bøger.
sentence.en: She is an author and has written three books.

en forklaring.explanation: "En forklaring" means "an explanation", what someone says to make a thing clear or to say why something happened. The action is at forklare (to explain).

sentence.da: Læreren gav en god **forklaring** på reglen.
sentence.en: The teacher gave a good explanation of the rule.

en forkølelse.explanation: "En forkølelse" means "a cold", the illness with a runny nose and a sore throat. In everyday talk, Danes more often say Jeg er forkølet (I have a cold). Do not mix it up with kold (cold in temperature).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **forkølelse** og ondt i halsen.
sentence.en: I have a cold and a sore throat.

en forlovelsesring.explanation: "En forlovelsesring" means "an engagement ring", the ring given when two people promise to marry.

sentence.da: Han gav hende en **forlovelsesring**, og hun sagde ja.
sentence.en: He gave her an engagement ring, and she said yes.

en forlygte.explanation: "En forlygte" means "a headlight", the light at the front of a car. It is built from for (front) and lygte (lamp), and for- also means front in et forsæde (a front seat).

sentence.da: Bilens **forlygte** lyser op på vejen.
sentence.en: The car's headlight lights up the road.

en forlystelsespark.explanation: "En forlystelsespark" means "an amusement park", a park with rides.

sentence.da: I en **forlystelsespark** kan man køre i rutsjebane.
sentence.en: In an amusement park you can ride a roller coaster.

en forlængerledning.explanation: "En forlængerledning" means "an extension cord". It is built from forlænge (to extend) and ledning (cord). Forlænge also works for time: at forlænge en aftale (to extend an agreement).

sentence.da: Der er langt til stikkontakten, men jeg har en **forlængerledning**.
sentence.en: It is far to the outlet, but I have an extension cord.

en form.explanation: "En form" means "a shape" and also "a baking pan": Huset har en rund form (The house has a round shape). Kagen bages i en form (The cake is baked in a pan). In Han er i god form (He is in good shape), it means fitness. A paper form is en blanket.

sentence.da: Kagen har en sjov **form**.
sentence.en: The cake has a funny shape.

en fornemmelse.explanation: "En fornemmelse" means "a feeling" or "a sense", more like a hunch than an emotion, because you cannot prove it. It can also be a bodily sensation: en fornemmelse af kulde (a sense of cold).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **fornemmelse** af, at han kommer i dag.
sentence.en: I have a feeling he is coming today.

en fornyelse.explanation: "En fornyelse" means "a renewal", making a passport, contract or membership valid again. It comes from at forny (to renew).

sentence.da: Jeg skal have en **fornyelse** af mit pas.
sentence.en: I need a renewal of my passport.

en fornøjelse.explanation: "En fornøjelse" means "a pleasure", for something nice you did or someone nice you met. It is also a polite reply to thanks: Fornøjelsen er min means "The pleasure is mine".

sentence.da: Det var en **fornøjelse** at arbejde med dig.
sentence.en: It was a pleasure to work with you.

en forret.explanation: "En forret" means "a starter", the small dish you eat before the main one. It comes first on a menu, and you order it with til forret (as a starter).

sentence.da: Jeg tager suppe til **forret**.
sentence.en: I will have soup as a starter.

en forretning.explanation: "En forretning" means "a business", and also "a shop". For a shop, en butik (a shop) is more common in everyday talk.

sentence.da: Min far har en lille **forretning** i byen.
sentence.en: My father has a small business in town.

en forrude.explanation: "En forrude" means "a windshield", the front window of a car. The back window is en bagrude (rear window).

sentence.da: Der er en lille revne i min **forrude**.
sentence.en: There is a small crack in my windshield.

en forsikring.explanation: "En forsikring" means "insurance", an arrangement where you pay a company so it covers a loss.

sentence.da: Vi har en **forsikring** på vores hus.
sentence.en: We have insurance on our house.

en forsinkelse.explanation: "En forsinkelse" means "a delay", the time something is later than planned, often for trains, buses and flights. To say something is late, use forsinket: Bussen er forsinket (The bus is late).

sentence.da: Toget har en **forsinkelse** på en time.
sentence.en: The train has a delay of one hour.

en forskel.explanation: "En forskel" means "a difference". To say between two things, use på: Der er en stor forskel på kaffe og te (There is a big difference between coffee and tea). To ask about it, say Hvad er forskellen? (What is the difference?).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke se nogen **forskel** på dem.
sentence.en: I can't see any difference between them.

en forstad.explanation: "En forstad" means "a suburb", an area of homes just outside a big city. It is built from for (in front of) and stad (town), so it lies in front of the town. Farther out than a forstad is landet (the countryside), as in at bo på landet (to live in the countryside).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **forstad** uden for København.
sentence.en: We live in a suburb outside Copenhagen.

en forstuvning.explanation: "En forstuvning" means "a sprain", from twisting a joint such as an ankle or wrist. The matching action is at forstuve (to sprain).

sentence.da: Hun fik en **forstuvning** og kan ikke gå.
sentence.en: She got a sprain and cannot walk.

en fortid.explanation: "En fortid" means "a past", the time that has already gone, in history or in your own life: Hun har en spændende fortid (She has an exciting past).

sentence.da: Han taler ikke om sin **fortid**.
sentence.en: He does not talk about his past.

en forårsdag.explanation: "En forårsdag" means "a spring day". It is built from forår (spring) and dag (day). I foråret means "in the spring".

sentence.da: Det er en dejlig **forårsdag**, og solen skinner.
sentence.en: It is a lovely spring day, and the sun is shining.

en forælder.explanation: "En forælder" means "a parent", one mother or father. You will more often hear the plural: Mine forældre bor i Aarhus (My parents live in Aarhus).

sentence.da: Som **forælder** vil man det bedste for sit barn.
sentence.en: As a parent you want the best for your child.

en fotograf.explanation: "En fotograf" means "a photographer", someone who takes pictures for a living.

sentence.da: Vi har brug for en **fotograf** til brylluppet.
sentence.en: We need a photographer for the wedding.

en frakke.explanation: "En frakke" means "a coat". It is longer and warmer than en jakke (a jacket). At tage frakken på means "to put the coat on".

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **frakke** på i kulden.
sentence.en: I put my coat on in the cold.

en franskmand.explanation: "En franskmand" means "a Frenchman" or "a French person". The country is Frankrig (France), and the language is fransk (French).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **franskmand**, og han bager godt brød.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a Frenchman, and he bakes good bread.

en fremmed.explanation: "En fremmed" means "a stranger", a person you do not know: Tal ikke med fremmede (Do not talk to strangers). Before another word, fremmed means "foreign": et fremmed land (a foreign country).

sentence.da: En **fremmed** bankede på døren i aftes.
sentence.en: A stranger knocked on the door last night.

en fremtid.explanation: "En fremtid" means "a future", the time that is still to come, for the world or for your own life.

sentence.da: Børnene skal have en god **fremtid**.
sentence.en: The children should have a good future.

en fridag.explanation: "En fridag" means "a day off", a day when you do not work or go to school. It is built from fri (free) and dag (day), and fri also works alone: Jeg har fri i dag (I am off today).

sentence.da: Min mand har **fridag** på onsdag.
sentence.en: My husband has a day off on Wednesday.

en frihed.explanation: "En frihed" means "a freedom", the right to decide for yourself: Ytringsfrihed er en vigtig frihed (Freedom of speech is an important freedom). The word fri (free) is in the same family.

sentence.da: Børn har brug for **frihed** til at lege.
sentence.en: Children need freedom to play.

en frikadelle.explanation: "En frikadelle" means "a meatball", a fried patty of minced meat. It is a classic Danish dish, eaten hot with potatoes or cold on rye bread.

sentence.da: Han steger en **frikadelle** af svinekød i panden.
sentence.en: He fries a pork meatball in the pan.

en frisør.explanation: "En frisør" means "a hairdresser", and it also means the place where you get a haircut: Jeg har tid hos frisøren means "I have an appointment at the hairdresser's". A barber, who cuts men's hair, is en barber.

sentence.da: Jeg skal til **frisør** i morgen.
sentence.en: I am going to the hairdresser tomorrow.

en frisørsalon.explanation: "En frisørsalon" means "a hair salon", the shop where you get your hair cut or colored.

sentence.da: Hun får klippet håret i en **frisørsalon**.
sentence.en: She gets her hair cut at a hair salon.

en frokostpause.explanation: "En frokostpause" means "a lunch break". It is built from frokost (lunch) and pause (break). Pause also stands alone: Skal vi holde en pause? (Shall we take a break?)

sentence.da: Vi holder **frokostpause** klokken tolv.
sentence.en: We take our lunch break at twelve.

en frugt.explanation: "En frugt" means "a fruit". For fruit in general, Danes usually leave out en: Jeg spiser meget frugt (I eat a lot of fruit). One piece of fruit is et stykke frugt.

sentence.da: Æbler og bananer er **frugt**.
sentence.en: Apples and bananas are fruit.

en frugthave.explanation: "En frugthave" means "an orchard", a garden with fruit trees. It is built from frugt (fruit) and have (garden). Have also looks like at have (to have), but en have is a garden.

sentence.da: Der vokser mange æbler i vores **frugthave**.
sentence.en: Many apples grow in our orchard.

en frugtsalat.explanation: "En frugtsalat" means "a fruit salad", cut fruit mixed together, often as a dessert.

sentence.da: Hun laver en **frugtsalat** med æbler og bananer.
sentence.en: She makes a fruit salad with apples and bananas.

en frugtskål.explanation: "En frugtskål" means "a fruit bowl", a bowl that holds fruit at home and often stands on the table. It is built from frugt (fruit) and skål (bowl). Skål is also what you say when you raise a glass: Skål! (Cheers!)

sentence.da: Der ligger tre æbler i en **frugtskål**.
sentence.en: There are three apples in a fruit bowl.

en frustration.explanation: "En frustration" means "a frustration", the feeling when things do not work out.

sentence.da: Det er en stor **frustration**, når bussen er forsinket.
sentence.en: It is a big frustration when the bus is late.

en frysepose.explanation: "En frysepose" means "a freezer bag", a strong bag for food that goes in the freezer.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger brødet i en **frysepose** og fryser det.
sentence.en: I put the bread in a freezer bag and freeze it.

en fryser.explanation: "En fryser" means "a freezer", the very cold part of a kitchen where food is stored frozen. The same spelling also appears in Jeg fryser (I am cold), which is about a person feeling cold.

sentence.da: Maden holder sig længe i en **fryser**.
sentence.en: Food keeps for a long time in a freezer.

en frø.explanation: "En frø" means "a frog". Et frø is a different word and means "a seed", so en or et changes the meaning.

sentence.da: En **frø** hopper rundt ved søen og kvækker.
sentence.en: A frog hops around by the lake and croaks.

en frøpose.explanation: "En frøpose" means "a seed packet", the small paper bag of seeds you buy for the garden. It is built from frø (seed) and pose (bag). Watch the article: et frø is a seed, but en frø is a frog.

sentence.da: Jeg købte en **frøpose** med gulerødder i dag.
sentence.en: I bought a seed packet with carrots today.

en fugl.explanation: "En fugl" means "a bird", an animal with feathers and wings that usually can fly.

sentence.da: Der sidder en **fugl** i træet og synger.
sentence.en: A bird is sitting in the tree and singing.

en fuglekasse.explanation: "En fuglekasse" means "a birdhouse", a small box that people hang in a tree as a home for birds.

sentence.da: Vi hængte en **fuglekasse** op i havens træ.
sentence.en: We hung up a birdhouse in the garden's tree.

en fugletur.explanation: "En fugletur" means "a birdwatching trip", a walk to look at birds. It is built from fugl (bird) and tur (trip). Tur also covers a short walk: at gå en tur (to go for a walk).

sentence.da: Vi tog på **fugletur** med kikkert tidligt om morgenen.
sentence.en: We went on a birdwatching trip with binoculars early in the morning.

en fugleunge.explanation: "En fugleunge" means "a baby bird", a young bird that is not grown yet. The last part, unge (a young one), is the word for the young of an animal.

sentence.da: Den lille **fugleunge** sidder i reden og piber.
sentence.en: The little baby bird sits in the nest and chirps.

en funktion.explanation: "En funktion" means "a function", what something does or is used for: Telefonen har mange funktioner (The phone has many functions). It can also mean a person's role: i funktion som leder (in the role of leader).

sentence.da: Knappen har en vigtig **funktion**.
sentence.en: The button has an important function.

en fyr.explanation: "En fyr" means "a guy" or "a fellow", and sounds casual: Han er en rar fyr (He is a nice guy). In a more formal way, say en mand (a man).

sentence.da: Min bror er en rigtig sjov **fyr**.
sentence.en: My brother is a really funny guy.

en fåreflok.explanation: "En fåreflok" means "a flock of sheep", a group of sheep that graze and move together. It is built from får (sheep) and flok (flock). Flok also works for people: en flok børn (a group of children).

sentence.da: Der går en stor **fåreflok** på marken.
sentence.en: A big flock of sheep is walking on the field.

en fælde.explanation: "En fælde" means "a trap", set for animals: en musefælde (a mousetrap). It can also be a trick set for a person: at gå i fælden means "to fall into the trap".

sentence.da: Han stillede en **fælde** op for musen.
sentence.en: He set up a trap for the mouse.

en færdselsregel.explanation: "En færdselsregel" means "a traffic rule", a rule for people on the road, whether they drive, bike or walk. You will more often hear the plural: færdselsregler (traffic rules).

sentence.da: At stoppe ved rødt lys er en **færdselsregel**.
sentence.en: Stopping at a red light is a traffic rule.

en færge.explanation: "En færge" means "a ferry", a boat that carries people and cars across the water.

sentence.da: Vi tager en **færge** over til øen.
sentence.en: We take a ferry over to the island.

en fætter.explanation: "En fætter" means "a male cousin", the son of your aunt or uncle. Danish has a separate word for a female cousin, en kusine, while English uses cousin for both.

sentence.da: Min **fætter** er søn af min mors bror.
sentence.en: My cousin is the son of my mother's brother.

en fødselsdag.explanation: "En fødselsdag" means "a birthday". The usual greeting is Tillykke med fødselsdagen! (Happy birthday!). Danes say Jeg har fødselsdag (literally I have birthday) where English says It is my birthday.

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fødselsdag** og får kage.
sentence.en: Today is my birthday, and I get cake.

en fødselsdagsfest.explanation: "En fødselsdagsfest" means "a birthday party", a party to celebrate someone's birthday, often at home with family and friends. It is built from fødselsdag (birthday) and fest (party). At the party, you say Tillykke med fødselsdagen! (Happy birthday!)

sentence.da: Vi har **fødselsdagsfest** med kage og gaver.
sentence.en: We have a birthday party with cake and presents.

en fødselsdagsgave.explanation: "En fødselsdagsgave" means "a birthday present", a gift for someone on their birthday. It is built from fødselsdag (birthday) and gave (gift). Gave also works in other gift words, like en bryllupsgave (a wedding gift).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **fødselsdagsgave** til min mor.
sentence.en: I am buying a birthday present for my mother.

en fødselsdagskage.explanation: "En fødselsdagskage" means "a birthday cake", the cake served to the guests at a birthday party. It is built from fødselsdag (birthday) and kage (cake). Kage also appears in en småkage (a cookie).

sentence.da: En **fødselsdagskage** har ofte lys på.
sentence.en: A birthday cake often has candles on it.

en fødselsdato.explanation: "En fødselsdato" means "a date of birth", the day, month and year you were born. It is not the same as en fødselsdag (a birthday), the day you celebrate each year.

sentence.da: Min **fødselsdato** er 12. marts 1990.
sentence.en: My date of birth is March 12, 1990.

en følelse.explanation: "En følelse" means "a feeling", such as joy or fear. It can also be a hunch: Jeg har en følelse af, at det går godt (I have a feeling that it will go well).

sentence.da: Kærlighed er en stærk **følelse**.
sentence.en: Love is a strong feeling.

en følger.explanation: "En følger" means "a follower", someone who follows your account online. It comes from at følge (to follow).

sentence.da: En **følger** kan se alle dine opslag.
sentence.en: A follower can see all your posts.

en føntørrer.explanation: "En føntørrer" means "a hairdryer". In everyday speech it is shortened to en føn, with the same meaning.

sentence.da: Mit hår er vådt, og jeg bruger en **føntørrer**.
sentence.en: My hair is wet, and I am using a hairdryer.

et fad.explanation: "Et fad" means "a dish", the large plate or bowl you serve food from. For your own food at the table, use en tallerken (a plate).

sentence.da: Hun lægger kødet på et **fad**.
sentence.en: She puts the meat on a dish.

et fadøl.explanation: "Et fadøl" means "a draft beer", beer poured from a tap instead of a bottle.

sentence.da: Vi tager hver et **fadøl** i baren.
sentence.en: We each have a draft beer at the bar.

et fag.explanation: "Et fag" means "a subject" at school. Put yndlings- (favorite) in front for your favorite: Mit yndlingsfag er historie (My favorite subject is history).

sentence.da: Matematik er et svært **fag**, men jeg kan lide det.
sentence.en: Math is a hard subject, but I like it.

et fald.explanation: "Et fald" means "a fall" and "a drop": et fald fra stigen (a fall from the ladder), et fald i priserne (a drop in prices). The matching verb is at falde (to fall).

sentence.da: Der har været et stort **fald** i temperaturen.
sentence.en: There has been a big drop in temperature.

et familiebillede.explanation: "Et familiebillede" means "a family photo", built from familie (family) and billede (picture). Billede covers any picture, not just photos.

sentence.da: Der hænger et **familiebillede** over sofaen.
sentence.en: A family photo hangs over the sofa.

et familiemedlem.explanation: "Et familiemedlem" means "a family member". Medlem alone is used for a member of a club: et medlem af klubben (a member of the club).

sentence.da: Hvert **familiemedlem** fik en gave.
sentence.en: Every family member got a gift.

et fartkamera.explanation: "Et fartkamera" means "a speed camera", a camera that takes a photo of cars that go too fast.

sentence.da: Jeg bremser, fordi der er et **fartkamera** ved vejen.
sentence.en: I brake because there is a speed camera by the road.

et felt.explanation: "Et felt" means "a field", but not a farm field. It is a box on a form: Skriv navnet i feltet (Write the name in the field). It can also be an area of work: Hun arbejder inden for dette felt (She works in this field).

sentence.da: Du skal udfylde hvert **felt** på siden.
sentence.en: You have to fill in every field on the page.

et feriested.explanation: "Et feriested" means "a vacation spot", a place people go to for a vacation.

sentence.da: Vi tager til et **feriested** ved havet i sommer.
sentence.en: We are going to a vacation spot by the sea this summer.

et firma.explanation: "Et firma" means "a company", a business that sells things or services.

sentence.da: Han har sit eget **firma** i Aarhus.
sentence.en: He has his own company in Aarhus.

et fitnesscenter.explanation: "Et fitnesscenter" means "a gym", a place with machines and weights.

sentence.da: Mange mennesker træner i et **fitnesscenter** efter arbejde.
sentence.en: Many people work out at a gym after work.

et fjernsyn.explanation: "Et fjernsyn" means "a television", the device. To talk about watching it, say Jeg ser fjernsyn (I watch TV), or just tv.

sentence.da: Vi ser film på vores store **fjernsyn**.
sentence.en: We watch movies on our big TV.

et flag.explanation: "Et flag" means "a flag", a piece of cloth that stands for a country or a group. To raise it, use at hejse (to hoist): Vi hejser flaget (We raise the flag).

sentence.da: Det danske **flag** er rødt med et hvidt kors.
sentence.en: The Danish flag is red with a white cross.

et fly.explanation: "Et fly" means "a plane". En flyvemaskine (an airplane) also exists, but it is longer, and et fly is the everyday word.

sentence.da: Vi sidder i et **fly** over skyerne.
sentence.en: We are sitting in a plane above the clouds.

et flyselskab.explanation: "Et flyselskab" means "an airline", a company that flies passengers. It is built from fly (plane) and selskab (company). Selskab also means a party: Der er selskab hos naboerne i aften (There is a party at the neighbors' tonight).

sentence.da: Hvilket **flyselskab** flyver du med?
sentence.en: Which airline are you flying with?

et fodgængerfelt.explanation: "Et fodgængerfelt" means "a crosswalk", the marked stripes where people cross the road. Danes also say fodgængerovergang (pedestrian crossing).

sentence.da: Børnene går over vejen ved et **fodgængerfelt**.
sentence.en: The children cross the road at a crosswalk.

et fodspor.explanation: "Et fodspor" means "a footprint", the mark a foot leaves. It is built from en fod (a foot) and et spor (a track). Spor also means a clue: Politiet leder efter spor (The police look for clues).

sentence.da: Der er et **fodspor** i sneen foran døren.
sentence.en: There is a footprint in the snow in front of the door.

et fokus.explanation: "Et fokus" means "a focus", what you pay the most attention to. You say fokus på (focus on) something: Vi har fokus på sundhed (We focus on health). To draw attention to something, say at sætte fokus på noget (to put focus on something).

forms.en: The focus is on the children.

sentence.da: Vi har **fokus** på vores kunder.
sentence.en: We focus on our customers.

et folk.explanation: "Et folk" means "a people", a whole nation: Det danske folk (The Danish people). Folk is also everyday talk for people in general: Der er mange folk her (There are lots of people here).

sentence.da: Det danske **folk** elsker at cykle.
sentence.en: The Danish people love to cycle.

et forhold.explanation: "Et forhold" means "a relationship", for example between two people: Jeg har et godt forhold til min søster (I have a good relationship with my sister). It also means how two things relate: Forholdet mellem pris og kvalitet er godt (The relation between price and quality is good).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **forhold** til min chef.
sentence.en: I have a good relationship with my boss.

et fornavn.explanation: "Et fornavn" means "a first name", the name you are given at birth, before the family name. It is made of for (before) and et navn (a name).

sentence.da: Mit **fornavn** er Anna.
sentence.en: My first name is Anna.

et forslag.explanation: "Et forslag" means "a suggestion" or "a proposal". You make one with at komme med et forslag (to come up with a suggestion): Har du et forslag? (Do you have a suggestion?).

sentence.da: Jeg har et godt **forslag** til middag.
sentence.en: I have a good suggestion for dinner.

et forsøg.explanation: "Et forsøg" means "an experiment", and also "an attempt": Det var et godt forsøg (That was a good attempt). In a lab, it is a test of an idea.

sentence.da: Vi laver et **forsøg** med vand og salt.
sentence.en: We do an experiment with water and salt.

et fortov.explanation: "Et fortov" means "a sidewalk", the part of a street for people on foot. Bikes use en cykelsti (a bike path).

sentence.da: Jeg går på et smalt **fortov** langs vejen.
sentence.en: I walk on a narrow sidewalk along the road.

et forår.explanation: "Et forår" means "a spring", the season between winter and summer when the flowers come out.

sentence.da: Det er **forår** med mange blomster.
sentence.en: It is spring with many flowers.

et foto.explanation: "Et foto" means "a photo". It is short for et fotografi (a photograph).

sentence.da: Jeg sendte hende et **foto** af hunden.
sentence.en: I sent her a photo of the dog.

et fotografi.explanation: "Et fotografi" means "a photograph", the longer word. In daily talk people often say et foto (a photo).

sentence.da: Fotografen tager et **fotografi** med sit kamera.
sentence.en: The photographer takes a photograph with his camera.

et frikvarter.explanation: "Et frikvarter" means "a recess" or "a break" between lessons. It is built from fri (free) and kvarter (quarter hour). Fri also starts en fridag (a day off).

sentence.da: Efter to timer har vi et **frikvarter**, og så leger vi.
sentence.en: After two lessons we have a recess, and then we play.

et frimærke.explanation: "Et frimærke" means "a stamp" for a letter. A rubber stamp for ink is et stempel, so do not mix them up.

sentence.da: Du skal sætte et **frimærke** på brevet.
sentence.en: You have to put a stamp on the letter.

et frø.explanation: "Et frø" means "a seed". Do not mix it up with en frø (a frog), which has a different word before it: Frøen hopper (The frog jumps).

sentence.da: Fra et lille **frø** vokser et stort træ.
sentence.en: A big tree grows from a small seed.

et fyrtårn.explanation: "Et fyrtårn" means "a lighthouse", a tall tower with a bright light that guides ships. It is built from fyr (beacon light) and tårn (tower). Fyr also means a guy: Han er en flot fyr (He is a handsome guy).

sentence.da: Om natten viser et **fyrtårn** skibene vej.
sentence.en: At night, a lighthouse shows the ships the way.

et får.explanation: "Et får" means "a sheep". Do not mix it up with får from at få (to get): Han får en gave means "He gets a gift".

sentence.da: Et **får** har uld og siger mæh.
sentence.en: A sheep has wool and says baa.

et fællesvaskeri.explanation: "Et fællesvaskeri" means "a shared laundry room", where all the residents of a building wash their clothes. Fælles means shared: Vi har et fælles køkken (We have a shared kitchen).

sentence.da: Der er et **fællesvaskeri** i huset, som alle bruger.
sentence.en: There is a shared laundry room in the building that everyone uses.

et fængsel.explanation: "Et fængsel" means "a prison", the building. To be in prison is to sidde i fængsel, without et: Han sidder i fængsel (He is in prison).

sentence.da: Han kom i **fængsel** i to år.
sentence.en: He went to prison for two years.

et fødested.explanation: "Et fødested" means "a birthplace", the town or country where someone was born. It is made of at føde (to give birth) and et sted (a place). You will see Fødested as a box on forms.

sentence.da: Mit **fødested** er Odense.
sentence.en: My birthplace is Odense.

faktisk.explanation: "Faktisk" means "actually" or "in fact". Use it when the truth is a bit different from what someone thinks: Det er faktisk nemt (It is actually easy).

sentence.da: Nej, han er **faktisk** dansk.
sentence.en: No, he is actually Danish.

falsk.explanation: "Falsk" means "fake", for things made to look real. For a person it means someone who only pretends to be nice: en falsk ven (a false friend).

sentence.da: Sedlen er **falsk**, og banken tager ikke imod den.
sentence.en: The bill is fake, and the bank will not accept it.

fantastisk.explanation: "Fantastisk" means "fantastic". It is stronger than god (good), so save it for something really great.

sentence.da: Maden var **fantastisk**!
sentence.en: The food was fantastic!

farlig.explanation: "Farlig" means "dangerous" and comes from fare (danger). Livsfarlig means "life-threatening".

sentence.da: Vejen er meget **farlig**.
sentence.en: The road is very dangerous.

farvel.explanation: "Farvel" means "goodbye". Danes often use hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you) for everyday goodbyes, while farvel sounds more final.

sentence.da: Jeg siger **farvel** til min ven.
sentence.en: I say goodbye to my friend.

fascinerende.explanation: "Fascinerende" means "fascinating", something that holds your attention and does not let go. For how you feel, use fascineret: Jeg er fascineret (I am fascinated).

sentence.da: Fuglenes liv er **fascinerende**, og jeg læser om dem.
sentence.en: The life of birds is fascinating, and I read about them.

fast.explanation: "Fast" means "fixed", for things that stay the same: en fast pris (a fixed price). It also means "steady" or "lasting": et fast job (a steady job).

sentence.da: Vi har en **fast** tid hver uge.
sentence.en: We have a set time every week.

fattig.explanation: "Fattig" means "poor", with little money, for people and also for countries. Stakkels also means "poor", but in the sense of unlucky: stakkels dig means "poor you".

sentence.da: Han er **fattig** og har næsten ingen penge.
sentence.en: He is poor and has almost no money.

fattigdom.explanation: "Fattigdom" means "poverty", the state of being poor. It is built from fattig (poor). The ending -dom also makes en sygdom (an illness) from syg (sick).

sentence.da: Mange børn lever i **fattigdom**.
sentence.en: Many children live in poverty.

februar.explanation: "Februar" means "February". Month names are written with a small letter: i februar (in February).

sentence.da: Efter januar kommer **februar**.
sentence.en: After January comes February.

fed.explanation: "Fed" means "cool" in casual speech: Det er fedt! (That is cool!) It also means "fat", as in fed mad (fatty food).

sentence.da: Wow, du har en **fed** cykel!
sentence.en: Wow, you have a cool bike!

fedt.explanation: "Fedt" means "fat", the kind in food. In casual talk it also means "cool": Det er fedt! (That is cool!)

sentence.da: Der er meget **fedt** i pommes frites.
sentence.en: There is a lot of fat in french fries.

fejlfri.explanation: "Fejlfri" means "flawless" or "without mistakes". It is built from fejl (mistake) and fri (free). The same -fri is in sukkerfri (sugar-free).

sentence.da: Teksten er **fejlfri**, og der er ingen stavefejl.
sentence.en: The text is flawless, and there are no spelling mistakes.

fem.explanation: "Fem" means "five". Fifty is not "femti" but halvtreds (fifty).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fem** fingre på hver hånd.
sentence.en: I have five fingers on each hand.

femogtredive.explanation: "Femogtredive" means "thirty-five". Danish says the five first: fem-og-tredive is literally five-and-thirty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 45, femogfyrre (five-and-forty).

sentence.da: Min bror er **femogtredive** år.
sentence.en: My brother is thirty-five years old.

femte.explanation: "Femte" means "fifth" and is used for order and dates: den femte marts (the fifth of March). Fem is the plain number: fem dage (five days), but den femte dag (the fifth day).

sentence.da: Min fødselsdag er den **femte** marts.
