sentence.en: My birthday is the fifth of March.

femten.explanation: "Femten" means "fifteen". Danes also say en kvart (a quarter of an hour) for fifteen minutes.

sentence.da: Der er **femten** elever i klassen.
sentence.en: There are fifteen students in the class.

feta.explanation: "Feta" means "feta", a white, salty cheese from Greece that crumbles easily.

sentence.da: Salaten smager godt med salt **feta** og agurk.
sentence.en: The salad tastes good with salty feta and cucumber.

fin.explanation: "Fin" means "fine" or "nice". It can also mean "fancy" or "elegant": en fin restaurant means "a fancy restaurant". Fint! on its own means "Great!" or "Okay, good!".

sentence.da: Solen skinner på en **fin** dag.
sentence.en: The sun shines on a nice day.

finland.explanation: "Finland" means "Finland", the Nordic country known for its thousands of lakes. Its capital is Helsinki.

sentence.da: **Finland** ligger øst for Sverige.
sentence.en: Finland lies east of Sweden.

finsk.explanation: "Finsk" means "Finnish" and describes things from Finland, including the language. It is written with a small letter, even for the language: Jeg taler finsk means "I speak Finnish".

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Finland og taler **finsk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Finland and speaks Finnish.

fint.explanation: "Fint" means "fine" or "nicely". It is a common answer to Hvordan går det? (How is it going?): Det går fint (It is going fine). Alone, Fint! means "Fine!" and agrees with a plan: Skal vi mødes klokken tre? Fint! (Shall we meet at three? Fine!).

sentence.da: Hvordan går det? Det går **fint**.
sentence.en: How is it going? It is going fine.

fire.explanation: "Fire" means "four": fire kroner (four kroner). Don't mix it up with fyrre (forty), which looks similar: fyrre kroner (forty kroner).

sentence.da: Hunden har **fire** ben.
sentence.en: The dog has four legs.

fireogtyve.explanation: "Fireogtyve" means "twenty-four". Danish says the four first: fire-og-tyve is literally four-and-twenty. The same goes for 25, femogtyve (five-and-twenty), and 26, seksogtyve (six-and-twenty).

sentence.da: Der er **fireogtyve** timer i et døgn.
sentence.en: There are twenty-four hours in a day.

firs.explanation: "Firs" means "eighty". It is short for firsindstyve (four times twenty). Sixty works the same way: tres (sixty) is three twenties.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er **firs** år gammel.
sentence.en: My grandfather is eighty years old.

fitness.explanation: "Fitness" means "fitness" in the sense of gym training. The place itself is et fitnesscenter (a gym). Being in good shape is not fitness in Danish, but i form (in shape).

sentence.da: Jeg dyrker **fitness** hver morgen før arbejde.
sentence.en: I do fitness every morning before work.

fjerde.explanation: "Fjerde" means "fourth" and is used for order and dates: den fjerde maj (the fourth of May). Fire is the plain number: fire dage (four days), but den fjerde dag (the fourth day).

sentence.da: Han sad i **fjerde** række.
sentence.en: He sat in the fourth row.

fjern.explanation: "Fjern" means "distant" or "remote", for places and times far away. It is also the start of fjernsyn (TV), literally a far-away view.

sentence.da: Han er en **fjern** fætter til mig.
sentence.en: He is a distant cousin of mine.

fjollet.explanation: "Fjollet" means "silly", playful and not serious: Stop med at være så fjollet (Stop being so silly). It is not harsh, so you can say it to a friend or a child.

sentence.da: Hun er **fjollet** og laver sjove grimasser.
sentence.en: She is silly and makes funny faces.

fjorten.explanation: "Fjorten" means "fourteen". Danes say fjorten dage (fourteen days) for "two weeks": Vi ses om fjorten dage (See you in two weeks).

sentence.da: Vi tager på ferie i **fjorten** dage.
sentence.en: We are going on vacation for fourteen days.

flad.explanation: "Flad" means "flat", with no bumps: Danmark er fladt (Denmark is flat). It also fits a tire with no air: Mit dæk er fladt (My tire is flat).

sentence.da: Stenen er **flad** og glat som en tallerken.
sentence.en: The stone is flat and smooth like a plate.

fleksibel.explanation: "Fleksibel" means "flexible" and describes a plan or a person that can change easily: Jeg er fleksibel i weekenden (I am flexible on the weekend). The opposite is stiv (stiff).

sentence.da: Min chef er **fleksibel** og lader mig arbejde hjemme.
sentence.en: My boss is flexible and lets me work from home.

flere.explanation: "Flere" means "more" or "several", for things you can count one by one: Jeg vil have flere kager (I want more cakes). For something you can't count, use mere: Jeg vil have mere kage (I want more cake), mere vand (more water).

sentence.da: Der er **flere** æbler end pærer i kurven.
sentence.en: There are more apples than pears in the basket.

flink.explanation: "Flink" means "kind" or "nice", for a helpful person: Han er flink (He is nice). With til, it means "good at": Hun er flink til matematik (She is good at math).

sentence.da: Naboen er **flink**, og han hjælper os ofte.
sentence.en: The neighbor is nice, and he often helps us.

flittig.explanation: "Flittig" means "diligent" and describes someone who works hard and steadily. The opposite is doven (lazy).

sentence.da: Hun er **flittig** og læser lektier hver dag.
sentence.en: She is diligent and does homework every day.

flot.explanation: "Flot" means "good-looking" or "impressive", for people, clothes, places and even results. Saying Flot! to someone means "Well done!".

sentence.da: Hun er smuk og har en **flot** kjole.
sentence.en: She is beautiful and has a nice-looking dress.

flov.explanation: "Flov" means "embarrassed", how you feel after a slip: Hun følte sig flov (She felt embarrassed). It describes you, not the situation. The situation is pinlig (embarrassing): Det var pinligt (That was embarrassing).

sentence.da: Jeg blev **flov**, da jeg glemte hans navn.
sentence.en: I got embarrassed when I forgot his name.

flydende.explanation: "Flydende" means "fluent" for speaking, and "liquid" for things you can pour. It is the same picture in both: speech or liquid that runs smoothly without stopping.

sentence.da: Efter to år taler hun **flydende** dansk.
sentence.en: After two years she speaks fluent Danish.

flæskesteg.explanation: "Flæskesteg" means "roast pork", a pork roast with crispy skin. It is built from flæsk (fatty pork) and en steg (a roast). En steg is any roast: en oksesteg (a beef roast).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **flæskesteg** med kartofler og sovs.
sentence.en: We eat roast pork with potatoes and gravy.

fløde.explanation: "Fløde" means "cream", the fatty part of milk, used in coffee, sauces and desserts. Piskefløde means "whipping cream" and is made of piske (to whip) and "fløde".

sentence.da: Vil du have **fløde** i kaffen?
sentence.en: Do you want cream in your coffee?

flødeost.explanation: "Flødeost" means "cream cheese", a soft white cheese for bread or cooking. It is fløde (cream) and ost (cheese) joined together.

sentence.da: Vi spiser brød med **flødeost** og laks.
sentence.en: We eat bread with cream cheese and salmon.

fodbold.explanation: "Fodbold" means "soccer". The game has no en in front: Jeg spiller fodbold means "I play soccer". En fodbold is the ball.

sentence.da: Børnene spiller **fodbold** og sparker til bolden.
sentence.en: The children play soccer and kick the ball.

folketinget.explanation: "Folketinget" means "the Danish Parliament", where the country's laws are made. For another country's parliament, say et parlament (a parliament).

sentence.da: **Folketinget** stemmer om den nye lov i dag.
sentence.en: The Parliament votes on the new law today.

for.explanation: "For" means "for", "too" or "ago", depending on the sentence. Compare Suppen er varm (The soup is hot) with Suppen er for varm (The soup is too hot). With siden (ago), it counts back in time: for to dage siden (two days ago). For a gift, Danish usually says til: en gave til dig (a gift for you).

sentence.da: Suppen er **for** varm.
sentence.en: The soup is too hot.

for det meste.explanation: "For det meste" means "mostly" and says that something is true in most cases. It is close to som regel (usually).

forms.da: Det er for det meste rart vejr.
Jeg læser for det meste om aftenen.
forms.en: I mostly read in the evening.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **for det meste** hjemme, men nogle gange ude.
sentence.en: We mostly eat at home, but sometimes out.

for eksempel.explanation: "For eksempel" means "for example". It goes right before the example: Jeg spiser meget frugt, for eksempel bananer (I eat a lot of fruit, for example bananas). In writing it is often shortened to fx (e.g.).

forms.da: Jeg kan godt lide frugt, for eksempel æbler.
forms.en: I like fruit, for example apples.

forms.da: Vi kan mødes, for eksempel i morgen.
forms.en: We can meet, for example tomorrow.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser frugt, **for eksempel** æbler.
sentence.en: I eat fruit, for example apples.

for evigt.explanation: "For evigt" means "forever", with no end. For a long wait, say Det tager en evighed (It takes forever).

sentence.da: Jeg vil huske dette sted **for evigt**.
sentence.en: I will remember this place forever.

for længe siden.explanation: "For længe siden" means "a long time ago": Han var her for længe siden (He was here a long time ago). Put a number in place of længe (long) to say exactly how long: for to år siden (two years ago).

forms.en: We met a long time ago
That was a long time ago

forms.da: Jeg boede der for længe siden
forms.en: I lived there a long time ago

sentence.da: Vi boede i Odense **for længe siden**.
sentence.en: We lived in Odense a long time ago.

for nylig.explanation: "For nylig" means "recently". It looks like for tiden (at the moment), but it points to the past, not to now.

forms.da: Jeg har for nylig købt en cykel
Vi har for nylig mødt ham

sentence.da: Jeg har **for nylig** købt en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I recently bought a new bike.

for pokker.explanation: "For pokker" means "darn it" or "for heaven's sake". It is a mild thing to say when something annoying or surprising happens.

forms.da: For pokker, jeg har glemt nøglen!
forms.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

sentence.da: **For pokker**, jeg har glemt nøglen!
sentence.en: Darn it, I forgot the key!

for søren.explanation: "For søren" means "oh dear" or "goodness" and shows surprise or mild annoyance.

forms.da: For søren, er klokken allerede otte?

sentence.da: **For søren**, hvor er det varmt i dag!
sentence.en: Goodness, it is so hot today!

for tiden.explanation: "For tiden" means "at the moment" or "these days", for something that is true now but may change. For this very second, say lige nu (right now).

forms.da: Jeg bor i Aarhus for tiden
forms.en: I live in Aarhus at the moment
She works from home at the moment
These days it rains a lot

sentence.da: Jeg arbejder hjemme **for tiden**.
sentence.en: I am working from home at the moment.

foran.explanation: "Foran" means "in front of". Compare Jeg står foran døren (I stand in front of the door) with Jeg står bag døren (I stand behind the door). Før (before) is only for time, not place: før klokken fem (before five o'clock).

sentence.da: Bilen holder **foran** huset.
sentence.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

forbi.explanation: "Forbi" means "past" or "by". Han gik forbi huset means "He walked past the house" (he did not stop). It also means "over": Sommeren er forbi (The summer is over). Kom forbi i aften! means "Drop by tonight!".

sentence.da: Bussen kører **forbi** skolen.
sentence.en: The bus drives past the school.

forbudt.explanation: "Forbudt" means "forbidden", for things the rules do not allow: Rygning er forbudt (Smoking is not allowed).

sentence.da: Det er **forbudt** at køre her.
sentence.en: It is forbidden to drive here.

fordi.explanation: "Fordi" means "because". It answers Hvorfor? (Why?): Hvorfor er du træt? (Why are you tired?) - Fordi jeg sover for lidt (Because I sleep too little). Do not mix it up with derfor (that is why): Jeg er træt, derfor går jeg i seng (I am tired, that is why I go to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg bliver hjemme **fordi** jeg er syg.
sentence.en: I stay home because I am sick.

forelsket.explanation: "Forelsket" means "in love", often the early, exciting stage: Jeg er forelsket i dig (I am in love with you). Use i (in) to say who the person is. At blive forelsket (to fall in love) is the moment it starts.

sentence.da: De er **forelsket** og smiler hele tiden.
sentence.en: They are in love and smile all the time.

forfra.explanation: "Forfra" means "from the beginning" and also "from the front": Kan vi tage det forfra? (Can we do it from the beginning?) Han kom bagfra (He came from behind) is the opposite of coming from the front.

sentence.da: Jeg tog fejl, og nu må jeg begynde **forfra**.
sentence.en: I made a mistake, and now I must begin again.

forfærdelig.explanation: "Forfærdelig" means "terrible" and is stronger than dårlig (bad): Det var en forfærdelig ulykke (It was a terrible accident).

sentence.da: Det var en **forfærdelig** ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: It was a terrible accident on the highway.

forhåbentlig.explanation: "Forhåbentlig" means "hopefully" and shows something you wish for: Forhåbentlig bliver det godt vejr (Hopefully the weather will be good). It says the same as Jeg håber, at det bliver godt vejr (I hope the weather will be good).

sentence.da: **Forhåbentlig** kommer toget til tiden i dag.
sentence.en: Hopefully the train comes on time today.

forkert.explanation: "Forkert" means "wrong" or "incorrect", for answers, directions, numbers or choices.

sentence.da: Fem plus fem er tolv. Det er **forkert**.
sentence.en: Five plus five is twelve. That is wrong.

forkølet.explanation: "Forkølet" means "having a cold". Jeg er forkølet means "I have a cold". It is milder than syg (sick).

sentence.da: Jeg er **forkølet** og hoster meget.
sentence.en: I have a cold and cough a lot.

forladt.explanation: "Forladt" means "abandoned": et forladt hus (an abandoned house). It also fits a person left alone: Han følte sig forladt (He felt abandoned).

sentence.da: Der står et **forladt** hus i skoven.
sentence.en: There is an abandoned house in the forest.

forlovet.explanation: "Forlovet" means "engaged" to marry: Jeg er forlovet med Anna (I am engaged to Anna). Use med (to) to say who the other person is.

sentence.da: Vi er **forlovet** og skal giftes næste år.
sentence.en: We are engaged and will get married next year.

fornuftig.explanation: "Fornuftig" means "sensible" and describes a choice or person that uses good sense: Det er fornuftigt at spare penge (It is sensible to save money). The opposite is dum (stupid).

sentence.da: Det er en **fornuftig** idé at tage en jakke med.
sentence.en: It is a sensible idea to bring a jacket.

forresten.explanation: "Forresten" means "by the way" and adds a thought that has just come to you: Forresten, har du set Mia? (By the way, have you seen Mia?).

forms.en: By the way, where do you live?
I know that, by the way.

sentence.da: **Forresten**, jeg har købt billetter til lørdag.
sentence.en: By the way, I have bought tickets for Saturday.

forrige.explanation: "Forrige" means "previous" and points to the one just before this one: i forrige måned (last month). It never changes: den forrige bil (the previous car), det forrige hus (the previous house).

sentence.da: Vi mødtes i **forrige** uge.
sentence.en: We met last week.

forsigtig.explanation: "Forsigtig" means "cautious" and describes someone who takes care to avoid risk: Han kører forsigtigt (He drives carefully). Vær forsigtig! is a common warning (Be careful!).

sentence.da: Vær **forsigtig**, gulvet er glat!
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery!

forsikring.explanation: "En forsikring" means "insurance", an agreement where you pay money regularly and the company pays for certain damage. To buy one, say at tegne en forsikring (to take out insurance).

sentence.da: Min **forsikring** dækker ikke vandskade.
sentence.en: My insurance does not cover water damage.

forsinket.explanation: "Forsinket" means "delayed" or "late", mostly for trains, buses and planes. About yourself you can also say Jeg er forsinket (I am late).

sentence.da: Toget er **forsinket** med tyve minutter.
sentence.en: The train is delayed by twenty minutes.

forskellig.explanation: "Forskellig" means "different", for things that are not alike: De to brødre er meget forskellige (The two brothers are very different). It also means "various": forskellige farver (various colors).

sentence.da: Vi har **forskellig** smag, men vi er gode venner.
sentence.en: We have different tastes, but we are good friends.

fortjent.explanation: "Fortjent" means "deserved" or "well earned", for something good you got because you worked for it.

sentence.da: Efter en lang uge er weekenden **fortjent**.
sentence.en: After a long week, the weekend is well deserved.

fortroligt.explanation: "Fortroligt" means "confidentially" or "in confidence", for things you tell one person who must keep them private: Jeg fortæller dig det fortroligt (I am telling you this in confidence). It also means "confidential": Dokumentet er fortroligt (The document is confidential).

forms.en: I am telling you this in confidence

sentence.da: Det er **fortroligt**. Sig det ikke til andre.
sentence.en: It is confidential. Do not tell anyone else.

forvirret.explanation: "Forvirret" means "confused", for when you do not understand what is going on.

sentence.da: Jeg er **forvirret**, fordi jeg ikke forstår det.
sentence.en: I am confused because I do not understand it.

forvirring.explanation: "Forvirring" means "confusion", when people do not understand what is going on. Someone who feels it is forvirret (confused): Jeg er helt forvirret (I am totally confused).

sentence.da: Der var **forvirring**, fordi alle talte på samme tid.
sentence.en: There was confusion because everyone talked at the same time.

forældre.explanation: "Forældre" means "parents", mother and father together. For just one parent, say en forælder (a parent).

sentence.da: Min mor og min far er mine **forældre**.
sentence.en: My mom and my dad are my parents.

fra.explanation: "Fra" means "from" and works for places, people and times. Its opposite is til (to): en gave til mig (a gift for me) versus en gave fra mig (a gift from me).

sentence.da: Toget kører **fra** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: The train goes from Copenhagen to Aarhus.

fra nu af.explanation: "Fra nu af" means "from now on" and looks forward, often for a new rule or decision. To look back instead, use indtil nu (until now).

forms.da: Fra nu af spiser jeg sundt.
forms.en: From now on I eat healthy.

forms.da: Fra nu af kommer jeg tidligt.
forms.en: From now on I come early.

forms.da: Fra nu af er det mit job.
forms.en: From now on it is my job.

sentence.da: Jeg går i seng klokken ti **fra nu af**.
sentence.en: I go to bed at ten from now on.

frankrig.explanation: "Frankrig" means "France", a large country in western Europe. It is written with a capital letter.

sentence.da: Paris ligger i **Frankrig**.
sentence.en: Paris is in France.

fransk.explanation: "Fransk" means "French", for things from France and for the language. It is written with a small letter: Jeg taler fransk (I speak French).

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Frankrig og taler **fransk**.
sentence.en: She comes from France and speaks French.

franskbrød.explanation: "Et franskbrød" means "a white loaf", the ordinary light kind. It is made of fransk (French) and brød (bread). Rugbrød (rye bread) is the dark, heavy kind.

sentence.da: **Franskbrød** er lyst og blødt brød.
sentence.en: White bread is light, soft bread.

fraskilt.explanation: "Fraskilt" means "divorced" and says what someone is now: Min onkel er fraskilt (My uncle is divorced). To talk about the event, say at blive skilt: De blev skilt i fjor (They got divorced last year).

sentence.da: Mine forældre er **fraskilt** og bor hver for sig.
sentence.en: My parents are divorced and live separately.

fred.explanation: "Fred" means "peace", the opposite of war and also a quiet, undisturbed time: Folk ønsker fred (People want peace). Lad mig være i fred (Leave me alone, literally "let me be in peace").

sentence.da: Landet har haft **fred** i mange år.
sentence.en: The country has had peace for many years.

fredag.explanation: "Fredag" means "Friday". På fredag means "on Friday" (the coming one) and om fredagen means "on Fridays" (every Friday). Day names are written with a small letter.

sentence.da: Efter torsdag kommer **fredag**.
sentence.en: After Thursday comes Friday.

fredelig.explanation: "Fredelig" means "peaceful" and describes calm places, people and times. It is built from fred (peace) and also fits a protest without fighting: en fredelig demonstration (a peaceful protest).

sentence.da: Landsbyen er stille og **fredelig**.
sentence.en: The village is quiet and peaceful.

fremmed.explanation: "Fremmed" means "foreign" or "strange": et fremmed sprog (a foreign language). On its own, en fremmed means "a stranger": Jeg talte med en fremmed (I talked to a stranger).

sentence.da: Det er et **fremmed** sprog for mig.
sentence.en: It is a foreign language to me.

fremtidig.explanation: "Fremtidig" means "future" and describes a person or thing that will be something later. The thing itself is fremtiden (the future): Vi tænker på fremtiden (We think about the future).

sentence.da: Hun er en **fremtidig** kollega.
sentence.en: She is a future colleague.

fri.explanation: "Fri" means "free" and also "off" from work or school: Jeg har fri means "I am off work". It does not mean free of charge; for that use gratis.

sentence.da: I dag har jeg **fri** fra arbejde.
sentence.en: Today I am off work.

frisk.explanation: "Frisk" means "fresh", for food and air. For a person it means "healthy": Jeg er frisk means "I am well".

sentence.da: Jeg købte mælken i dag. Den er **frisk**.
sentence.en: I bought the milk today. It is fresh.

fritid.explanation: "Fritid" means "free time", the time when you are not at work or school.

sentence.da: I min **fritid** går jeg ture.
sentence.en: In my free time I go for walks.

sentence.da: Klokken er tolv. Vi spiser **frokost**.
sentence.en: It is twelve o'clock. We eat lunch.

frossen.explanation: "Frossen" means "frozen", food that has been kept so cold that it is hard. For a person who feels cold, do not use it: Danes say jeg fryser (I am cold, literally I freeze).

sentence.da: Pizzaen i fryseren er **frossen**.
sentence.en: The pizza in the freezer is frozen.

frost.explanation: "Frost" means "frost", the cold when it is below freezing outside: Der er frost i nat (There is frost tonight). It also means the white ice on a window: Der er frost på ruden (There is frost on the window).

sentence.da: Når der er **frost**, fryser vandet til is.
sentence.en: When there is frost, the water freezes to ice.

frustreret.explanation: "Frustreret" means "frustrated", the feeling when things do not work out: Jeg er frustreret over computeren (I am frustrated with the computer). Det er frustrerende (It is frustrating) describes the thing itself.

sentence.da: Han er **frustreret**, fordi printeren ikke virker.
sentence.en: He is frustrated because the printer does not work.

frygt.explanation: "Frygt" means "fear": Hun følte frygt (She felt fear). To say you are afraid, use bange: Jeg er bange (I am afraid).

sentence.da: Hun kunne ikke skjule sin **frygt**.
sentence.en: She could not hide her fear.

frygtelig.explanation: "Frygtelig" means "terrible", for something awful or scary.

sentence.da: Stormen var **frygtelig**, og træer faldt om.
sentence.en: The storm was terrible, and trees fell over.

fræk.explanation: "Fræk" means "cheeky" or "naughty", often for a child who tests the limits: Hvor er du fræk! (How cheeky you are!). It also fits a daring joke: en fræk vittighed (a naughty joke).

sentence.da: Den lille dreng var meget **fræk** i dag.
sentence.en: The little boy was very naughty today.

fugtig.explanation: "Fugtig" means "damp" or "humid", for towels, walls and air: Håndklædet er fugtigt (The towel is damp). It is not the same as våd (wet), which means soaked.

sentence.da: Luften i badeværelset er meget **fugtig**.
sentence.en: The air in the bathroom is very humid.

fugtigt.explanation: "Fugtigt" means "humid" for air and "damp" for things: Håndklædet er stadig fugtigt (The towel is still damp). It is only a little wet, not the same as vådt (wet).

sentence.da: Der er **fugtigt** i kælderen.
sentence.en: It is damp in the basement.

fuld.explanation: "Fuld" means "full", for a glass, a bus or a room. When it describes a person, it means "drunk": Han er fuld means "He is drunk". To say you are full after a meal, use mæt (full after eating).

sentence.da: Bussen er helt **fuld** af mennesker.
sentence.en: The bus is completely full of people.

fuldkorn.explanation: "Fuldkorn" means "whole grain", the whole seed of the grain, used in bread and pasta: Jeg vælger fuldkorn (I choose whole grain). Added to another word, it describes it: fuldkornspasta (whole-grain pasta).

sentence.da: **Fuldkorn** er sundt, fordi det har mange fibre.
sentence.en: Whole grain is healthy because it has a lot of fiber.

fuldstændig.explanation: "Fuldstændig" means "completely" and makes a word as strong as it can be: Hun har fuldstændig ret (She is completely right). It also describes things that miss nothing: et fuldstændigt svar (a complete answer).

sentence.da: Jeg har **fuldstændig** glemt hans navn.
sentence.en: I have completely forgotten his name.

fuldt booket.explanation: "Fuldt booket" means "fully booked", with nothing free left. For tickets to a show, say udsolgt (sold out).

forms.da: Vi er fuldt booket i juli
forms.en: We are fully booked in July

sentence.da: Desværre er hotellet **fuldt booket** i weekenden.
sentence.en: Unfortunately, the hotel is fully booked this weekend.

fyldt.explanation: "Fyldt" means "full" or "filled", for something that has been filled up. For a person who has eaten enough, use mæt (full).

sentence.da: Hans lommer er **fyldt** med slik.
sentence.en: His pockets are filled with candy.

fyrre.explanation: "Fyrre" means "forty". Do not mix it up with fire (four): fire kroner is four kroner, fyrre kroner is forty kroner. For 41, you say enogfyrre, literally one-and-forty.

sentence.da: Jeg er **fyrre** år gammel.
sentence.en: I am forty years old.

fyrværkeri.explanation: "Fyrværkeri" means "fireworks" and is used for the whole display. For one single rocket, say en raket (a rocket).

sentence.da: **Fyrværkeri** lyser op på nattehimlen.
sentence.en: Fireworks light up the night sky.

fysik.explanation: "Fysik" means "physics", the study of forces, light and energy. For a school class, you leave out en: Jeg har fysik efter frokost (I have physics after lunch).

sentence.da: I **fysik** lærer vi om lys og lyd.
sentence.en: In physics we learn about light and sound.

fysisk.explanation: "Fysisk" means "physical", about the body or about real things you can touch: fysisk arbejde (physical work). Et fysisk møde (an in-person meeting) happens in real life, not online.

sentence.da: Løb og svømning er god **fysisk** træning.
sentence.en: Running and swimming are good physical exercise.

fælles.explanation: "Fælles" means "shared" or "common", for what belongs to several people together: Vi har et fælles køkken (We have a shared kitchen). It also fits a person two people both know.

sentence.da: Vi har en **fælles** ven i Aarhus.
sentence.en: We have a mutual friend in Aarhus.

færdig.explanation: "Færdig" means "finished" or "done", for example after a meal or at the end of work. Do not mix it up with klar (ready), which means prepared to start: Er du klar? (Are you ready?).

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet brevet. Nu er jeg **færdig**.
sentence.en: I have written the letter. Now I am done.

færdig med.explanation: "Færdig med" means "finished with". After med (with) you put the thing (færdig med lektierne, finished with the homework) or an action starting with at (færdig med at spise, finished eating).

forms.en: Are you finished with the book?

forms.da: Vi er færdige med at spise.

sentence.da: Nu er jeg **færdig med** arbejdet.
sentence.en: Now I am finished with work.

færre.explanation: "Færre" means "fewer" and goes with things you can count: færre biler (fewer cars). For something you cannot count, use mindre (less): mindre støj (less noise).

sentence.da: Der er **færre** stole end gæster.
sentence.en: There are fewer chairs than guests.

føj.explanation: "Føj" means "yuck" and shows disgust at a smell, a taste or something dirty: Føj, det lugter forfærdeligt! (Yuck, that smells awful!). Parents also say it to children: Føj, læg den fra dig (Yuck, put it down).

sentence.da: **Føj**, der er en edderkop i badekarret!
sentence.en: Yuck, there is a spider in the bathtub!

følgende.explanation: "Følgende" means "following", the next thing in a list or in time: Læs følgende tekst (Read the following text). The word looks the same with en-words, et-words and plurals.

sentence.da: Den **følgende** dag skinnede solen igen.
sentence.en: The following day the sun shone again.

følsom.explanation: "Følsom" means "sensitive" and is used for people who feel things strongly, and for skin or things that react easily: Hun er følsom over for kritik (She is sensitive to criticism). Jeg har følsom hud (I have sensitive skin).

sentence.da: Han er **følsom** og græder let ved triste film.
sentence.en: He is sensitive and cries easily at sad movies.

før.explanation: "Før" means "before" in time. For place, use foran (in front of): foran huset (in front of the house).

sentence.da: Klokken fire er **før** klokken fem.
sentence.en: Four o'clock is before five o'clock.

først.explanation: "Først" means "first" or "not until". Jeg kommer først i morgen means "I am not coming until tomorrow". Do not mix it up with første (the first one): den første dag (the first day).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **først** og går bagefter.
sentence.en: We eat first and go afterwards.

først og fremmest.explanation: "Først og fremmest" means "first and foremost". It introduces the most important point, so what comes after it matters most.

forms.da: Først og fremmest skal du hvile.
forms.en: First and foremost, you must rest.

sentence.da: **Først og fremmest** skal du hvile dig.
sentence.en: First and foremost, you need to rest.

første.explanation: "Første" means "first" in a list or order. It is used in dates: den første maj (the first of May), written 1. maj. Do not mix it up with først, which tells when something happens: Først spiser vi (First we eat).

sentence.da: Januar er årets **første** måned.
sentence.en: January is the first month of the year.

førstehjælp.explanation: "Førstehjælp" means "first aid", the help you give right away to someone who is hurt. It is built from første (first) and hjælp (help). The kit you keep at home is en førstehjælpskasse (a first aid box).

sentence.da: Man giver **førstehjælp**, når nogen kommer til skade.
sentence.en: You give first aid when someone gets hurt.
